9.grammar: A verbal noun (the act itself). The '-an' ending (indefinite 'tanwīn') is the accusative case; in this kind of word it often functions adverbially, describing the manner of an action ('… by way of guesswork / as conjecture'). The indefinite sense comes from the nunation.
9.root: ر-ج-م (r-j-m) — to stone, pelt; to conjecture

10.meaning: 'In the unseen' — the preposition 'in/by' with 'the unseen': that which is hidden from perception, beyond what the senses can reach (such as Allah, the angels, and the Hereafter). It denotes the realm one cannot directly observe yet may affirm.
10.grammar: A preposition bi- joined to a definite masculine singular noun. The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition — hence 'in the unseen'. The article al- makes it 'the unseen' as a known whole rather than 'an unseen thing'.
10.root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b) — being hidden, absent from sight

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they say / and they keep saying' — to utter or assert in speech. The structure presents an ongoing or repeated act of speaking by a group.
11.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb joined by wa- ('and'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks the 3rd-person masculine plural ('they'); the full -ūna ending is the inseparable indicative-plural suffix, showing the verb is in its base (indicative) form and expressing an ongoing or habitual action.
11.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

12.meaning: The cardinal number 'seven' (in its feminine-form shape used when counting masculine items).
12.grammar: A number-noun. The '-un' ending (indefinite 'tanwīn') is the nominative case, the default form used for a subject or a predicate ('they are seven'). The '-at' (tied-tāʾ) is the feminine spelling that Arabic uses for the numbers 3–10 when the counted things are masculine.
12.root: س-ب-ع (s-b-ʿ) — seven

13.meaning: A compound ordinal with a connector: 'and the eighth of them' — the position-eight member among a group, joined by 'and.'
13.grammar: The connector 'wa-' ('and') prefixed to an ordinal number ('eighth') in the active-participle pattern, with an attached pronoun. The '-u' ending is the nominative case (default for a subject or predicate). The suffix '-hum' is 'them/of them' (masculine plural), keeping its 'u' vowel after the nominative '-u'; it links the ordinal to the group ('the eighth of them').
13.root: ث-م-ن (th-m-n) — eight

14.meaning: A compound: 'their dog' — the animal 'dog' joined to the possessive pronoun 'their.'
14.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The '-u' ending is the nominative case (the default form for a subject or predicate). The suffix '-hum' means 'their' (masculine plural); it keeps its 'u' vowel because it follows the nominative '-u.'

15.meaning: An imperative command meaning 'Say!' or 'Speak!' — a direct order to one person to utter or declare something.
15.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male. The bare, vowelless ending (the silent stop on the final 'l') marks it as a direct order: 'you, say!' It is built from the verb 'to say' with the weak middle letter dropped, leaving the short, clipped command form.
15.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

16.meaning: 'My Lord' — the word 'rabb' denotes the Lord, Master, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, owns, governs and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached 'my' it expresses one's own Lord and Caretaker.
16.grammar: A noun followed by the possessive ending '-ī' meaning 'my', which joins to the noun and also serves the genitive (possessive) relationship. The attached '-ī' both makes the noun definite and shows ownership: 'my Lord'.
16.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, sustaining

17.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
17.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.
17.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowing, knowledge

18.meaning: A compound: 'of/by their number' — the noun 'ʿiddah' (a count, number, or tally) governed by a preposition and joined to the pronoun 'their.'
18.grammar: The preposition 'bi-' ('with/by/of') prefixed to a noun that carries a possessive pronoun. A preposition forces the genitive case, shown by the '-i' before the pronoun. The suffix '-him' is 'their' (masculine plural); its vowel is 'i' (and not '-hum') because it follows that genitive '-i.' The tied-tāʾ of 'ʿiddah' is pronounced 't' here because the word is joined to what follows.

19.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
19.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
19.root: — (particle; no root)

20.meaning: 'He knows them / He recognises them'. From the verb 'to know', with attached 'them' — having full knowledge or awareness of those persons.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The -u ending is the base (indicative) mood, used for an ongoing or habitual action. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them'.

21.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
21.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

22.meaning: Few, little, scant, or small in amount — the opposite of many or much.
22.grammar: An adjective/noun on the 'faʿīl' pattern (denoting a quality). The '-un' ending (indefinite 'tanwīn') is the nominative case, the default form for a subject or predicate ('… are few'). 'A few,' indefinite, comes from the nunation.

23.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
23.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

24.meaning: To dispute, argue, or contend over something — a back-and-forth wrangling, in the shortened form that a verb takes after a prohibition ('do not argue').
24.grammar: A present-tense verb in the 'mutual-effort' pattern (Form III), which carries the sense of contending with another party. The 'tu-' prefix marks a second-person 'you' subject. The bare final '-i' (with the weak final root-letter dropped) is the shortened jussive/apocopate form, which is the shape any imperfect verb is required to take after the prohibitive particle 'lā' ('do not').

25.meaning: "in them / among them" — the preposition 'in/among' joined to the pronoun 'them,' locating something within or amid a group of people.
25.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun, giving 'fīhim.' The preposition 'fī' keeps its long 'ī.' The pronoun '-him' is the third-person masculine plural ('them'); its vowel is 'i' (rather than '-hum') because it follows the high front vowel 'ī' of 'fī'.
25.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

26.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
26.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

27.meaning: A dispute, argument, or contention — the verbal noun naming the act of arguing/wrangling itself.
27.grammar: A verbal noun (the act itself, from the Form III 'contending' pattern). The '-an' ending (indefinite 'tanwīn,' here written on the final hamza/alif) is the accusative case; such a noun frequently specifies the kind or manner of the action ('argue with [only] a … kind of arguing'). The indefiniteness comes from the nunation.

28.meaning: Outward, apparent, visible, or plain — that which shows on the surface and is openly evident; also 'prevailing/uppermost.'
28.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer/quality' word — 'one that is showing/apparent'). The '-an' ending (indefinite 'tanwīn') is the accusative case, the form taken by a descriptive complement or object describing how something is ('… in a plain/outward manner'). The indefiniteness comes from the nunation.
28.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — to be outward, appear, become manifest

29.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
29.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

30.meaning: To seek a ruling, opinion, or information; to ask/consult — to request that someone clarify or pronounce on a matter, in the shortened form that a verb takes after a prohibition ('do not ask/consult').

parts.en: to seek a ruling / consult (Form X stem)

30.grammar: A present-tense verb in the 'seeking/requesting' pattern (Form X, marked by the 'sta-' element), giving the sense 'to ask someone for a verdict or clarification.' The 'ta-' prefix marks a second-person 'you' subject. The bare final '-i' (with the weak final root-letter dropped) is the shortened jussive/apocopate form, which is the shape any imperfect verb is required to take after the prohibitive particle 'lā' ('do not').
30.root: ف-ت-ي (f-t-y) — to give a formal opinion/verdict; youthful vigor

31.meaning: "in them / among them" — the preposition 'in/among' joined to the pronoun 'them,' locating something within or amid a group of people.
31.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun, giving 'fīhim.' The preposition 'fī' keeps its long 'ī.' The pronoun '-him' is the third-person masculine plural ('them'); its vowel is 'i' (rather than '-hum') because it follows the high front vowel 'ī' of 'fī'.
31.root: — (preposition; the pronoun has no triliteral root)

32.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
32.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

33.meaning: One; a single one; anyone — and in negative/prohibitive contexts, 'anyone at all / no one.'
33.grammar: A noun meaning 'one/anyone.' The '-an' ending (indefinite 'tanwīn') is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb ('ask anyone'). When such a verb is negated or prohibited, 'aḥadan' carries the sense 'anyone at all.' The indefiniteness comes from the nunation.

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: An emphatic '(do not) say' — the act of saying/speaking stated with strong emphasis, the shape used in a forceful prohibition ('never say').
2.grammar: A present-tense verb carrying the heavy emphatic ending '-nna' (the 'nūn of emphasis'), which intensifies the verb — typically paired with a prohibitive 'do not' to mean 'do not ever / never say.' The 'ta-' prefix marks a second-person 'you' subject. The 'a' vowel before the '-nna' belongs to this emphatic conjugation.
2.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

3.meaning: "of a thing" / "of anything" — the indefinite noun for any single item, matter, object, or affair, here governed by a preceding preposition meaning "with respect to / concerning a thing".
3.grammar: The prefix li- is a preposition ("to / for / regarding"). The noun carries the ending -in (tanwīn kasra), which marks it as indefinite ("a thing / any thing") and genitive — the case required after a preposition; the -in (an "i"-type ending) signals this governed, "of/for a thing" relationship.

4.meaning: 'Truly I' or 'indeed I' — the emphatic affirming particle inna ('truly, indeed, certainly'), which strengthens and confirms a statement, joined to the pronoun 'I'.
4.grammar: An emphasizing particle with an attached pronoun. 'Inna' is a particle of emphasis and affirmation that introduces a statement and lends it certainty ('it is certainly the case that…'). The attached -ī is the first-person singular pronoun ('I / me') in the object form this particle requires. Together: 'Indeed I…'.

5.meaning: "one who does / a doer" — the active participle naming the agent who performs or carries out an action; describes the one actually doing something.
5.grammar: This is the active-participle pattern fāʿil ("the one doing X"), built on the simple verb "to do/make". The ending -un (tanwīn ḍamma) marks it as indefinite ("a doer") and nominative — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate; the "u"-type ending signals this naming/subject function.
5.root: ف-ع-ل (f-ʿ-l) — doing, making, acting

6.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
6.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

7.meaning: 'Tomorrow', and more broadly 'the (coming) morning' or 'a day soon to come'. It points to the near future, the next day.
7.grammar: A noun used adverbially for time. The -an ending (with tanwīn, the doubled 'n' sound) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative state, which is the typical form for an adverb of time ('on the morrow, tomorrow').
7.root: غ-د-و (gh-d-w) — morning, the early part of the day, going forth in the morning

1.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
2.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
2.root: — (particle; no root)

3.meaning: '(that) he wills / wishes' — to will, intend, or so desire that a thing comes about.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine singular ('he wills'). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which typically appears after particles meaning 'that/so that/until,' giving the sense 'that he should will.'

4.meaning: Allah — the proper name of the One God: the sole, eternal Creator and Sustainer, unique and without partner, the object of all worship.
4.grammar: The unique proper name of the Deity (al-lāh, 'the God'). The final '-u' is the nominative case, the form typically used when the name is the subject of a sentence — the one performing the action.

5.meaning: And remember / call to mind / mention — a command to bring something to mind, keep it in remembrance, or speak of it; in religious usage it carries the sense of mindful, devotional remembrance.
5.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one male, 'remember!' / 'mention!', prefixed by 'and'. The vowelless ending (sukūn on the final r) is the normal form of a singular masculine command.
5.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember, mention, call to mind

6.meaning: Your Lord — Rabb denotes the Lord, Master, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, owns, and continually cares for and brings to maturity all that He governs; here addressed to a single male possessor.
6.grammar: A masculine noun with the accusative -a ending (commonly marking the object of a verb) plus the possessive suffix -ka ('your', one male). Rabb is a rich term — far more than 'lord' in the social sense — combining ownership, authority, and nurturing care.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, sustain, master, lord over

7.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

8.meaning: "you forgot" / "you became forgetful" — to fail to recall something, to let it slip from mind, or to neglect it.
8.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The suffix -ta marks the doer as "you" (single male addressee) and signals completed action — "you (have) forgot". The fixed -a vowel on this -ta ending is the standard marker for a masculine "you" subject in the past tense.

9.meaning: And say! / so say!: a command to one person to speak, joined to what precedes by 'and'.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male, 'say!', prefixed with the conjunction 'wa-' ('and'). The bare, vowel-less ending is the normal form for this imperative.
9.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak

10.meaning: It may be that / perhaps — a verb of approximation expressing hopeful expectation or near-likelihood that something will come about. When used of Allah it conveys an outcome that is sure to be realized rather than mere doubt.
10.grammar: A verb of approximation (one of the 'verbs of hoping/nearness'), defective and non-conjugating: it stays fixed in this form and does not change for tense or person. Its final -ā reflects the underlying weak root letter. It introduces an expected or hoped-for possibility, typically followed by a clause stating what may occur.
10.root: ع-س-و / ع-س-ي (ʿ-s-w/y) — to be hoped for, to be near (verb of approximation/hope)

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
11.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
11.root: — (particle; no root)

12.meaning: "that He may guide me" / "He will guide me" — to lead, direct, or show the right way, with the action aimed at the speaker ("me").
12.grammar: A present/future verb. The prefix ya- marks the doer as "he". The final -a on the stem (hdiya) is the subjunctive mood, typically triggered by a preceding particle of hope, purpose, or expectation ("that He may…"). The attached -ni is the object pronoun "me" (the protective nūn al-wiqāya before the suffix).
12.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way

13.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
13.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
13.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

14.meaning: "to (something) nearer / closer" — the comparative form "nearer, more proximate," describing greater closeness in distance, kinship, time, or likeness.
14.grammar: The prefix li- is a preposition ("to/toward"). The word follows the elative/comparative pattern afʿal ("more/most near"). Its ending is -a (fatḥa, the genitive marker used for diptotes — words that resist the usual -i ending), which here marks the genitive case required after the preposition.

15.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
15.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
15.root: — (preposition)

16.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
16.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

17.meaning: Right guidance, sound direction, maturity of judgment — being on a straight and correct course, the opposite of error or folly.
17.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending is the accusative with 'tanwīn' (the doubled-fatḥa nunation), which generally marks a word as an object of a verb, or as an adverbial/specifying complement ('... in the way of right guidance'). The tanwīn signals the noun is indefinite ('right guidance' in general).
17.root: ر-ش-د (r-sh-d) — right guidance, sound judgment, maturity

1.meaning: "and they stayed / remained / tarried" — to abide, dwell, or linger in a place or state for a span of time.
1.grammar: The prefix wa- is the connector "and". The verb is past tense (perfect), and the suffix -ū marks the doer as "they" (a group, masculine plural) and signals completed action — "they remained". The silent alif after -ū is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
2.root: — (particle)

3.meaning: "their cave" — a hollow or cavern in a mountain large enough to shelter people.
3.grammar: A noun with the -i (genitive) ending, marking it as possessed or as following a preposition ("… of …"). The attached -him is a possessive pronoun, "their," referring to a group of males.
3.root: ك-ه-ف (k-h-f) — a cave, cavern, mountain hollow

4.meaning: "three" — the cardinal number 3.
4.grammar: A cardinal number. The ending -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case; numbers in this construct state precede the thing counted and link to it ("three of …"), with the counted noun following in the genitive. The -a is the case ending shown in the transliteration.

5.meaning: "a hundred" — the cardinal number 100.
5.grammar: A cardinal number (100). The ending -in (tanwīn kasra) marks it as indefinite and genitive — the "i"-type ending appearing because it stands as the counted noun governed by a preceding number ("… of a hundred"). The internal spelling with alif (mi-ah) is conventional.
5.root: م-أ-ي (m-ʾ-y) — hundred

6.meaning: 'Years' — the plural of sana (a year). It refers to a span of multiple years, often a succession of seasons or yearly cycles.
6.grammar: A sound masculine-type plural noun. The -īna ending (here -īn + a) is the form used when the noun is the object of a verb or follows a preposition (accusative/genitive case), as opposed to -ūna for the subject case.

7.meaning: "and they increased / added" — to grow more, to add to an amount, or to exceed; from the reflexive pattern, "they added (further) to themselves."
7.grammar: The prefix wa- is "and". The verb is a past-tense (perfect) form of the eighth (reflexive) pattern built on "increase" (the t of that pattern has assimilated into the z). The suffix -ū marks the doer as "they" (masculine plural) and signals completed action. The opening alif is a connecting (elidable) hamza, pronounced only when starting fresh.

8.meaning: "nine" — the cardinal number 9.
8.grammar: A cardinal number (9). The ending -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite and accusative — an "a"-type ending that often signals a noun functioning as an object or as a specifying complement ("nine more"). The written alif carries the tanwīn.

1.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
2.root: — (proper divine name)

3.meaning: 'I know' — a present-tense verb of knowing: to have certain knowledge or awareness of something.
3.grammar: A present/future (Form I) verb, first-person singular ('I'), marked by the prefix a-. This a- is the first-person agreement marker built into the conjugation, not a free-standing pronoun. The final -u marks the indicative — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual knowing.

4.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
4.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

5.meaning: A past-tense statement meaning 'they stayed / remained / tarried' — to abide somewhere for a stretch of time.
5.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb. The -ū ending is the attached subject pronoun 'they' for a group of males. (The silent alif written after it is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.)
5.root: ل-ب-ث (l-b-th) — to stay, remain, tarry, abide

6.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
6.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

7.meaning: The unseen — all that is hidden from the senses and lies beyond human perception, known fully only to Allah.
7.grammar: A verbal noun meaning 'that which is hidden, the unseen.' The final -u is nominative, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the unseen OF …').

8.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
8.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

9.meaning: 'And the earth' — the connective 'and' joined to 'the earth', meaning the ground, land, or the world beneath the sky.
9.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') with the definite feminine noun 'al-arḍ' ('the earth'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the earth') or follows a preposition, here matching the case of what it is joined to.
9.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land

10.meaning: "how clearly He sees!" / "make (it) seen!" — an exclamatory form expressing wonder at how perfectly someone perceives or sees; from the causative "to make see / perceive sharply."
10.grammar: This is the "verb of wonder/amazement" pattern afʿil (identical in form to a command). It expresses astonishment — "how clearly/perfectly He perceives!" The fixed sukūn (no vowel) on the final consonant is invariable for this exclamatory/imperative form; it does not change for case.
10.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — sight, seeing, insight

11.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
11.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

12.meaning: "and how clearly He hears!" / "and make (it) heard!" — an exclamatory form expressing wonder at how perfectly someone hears; from the causative "to make hear."
12.grammar: The prefix wa- is "and". The rest is the "verb of wonder" pattern afʿil (same form as a command), expressing amazement — "how clearly/perfectly He hears!" The final consonant takes an invariable sukūn (no vowel), fixed for this exclamatory/imperative form regardless of case.
12.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

13.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
13.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

14.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
14.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

15.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
15.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

16.meaning: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

parts.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

16.grammar: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.
16.root: — (no triliteral root; a relational particle/noun)

17.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
17.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
17.root: — (preposition)

18.meaning: "a protecting friend / guardian / patron" — one who is intimately near and takes charge of another's affairs: a helper, ally, protector, or guardian; also a close devoted friend.
18.grammar: A noun of the faʿīl pattern (doubled final yāʾ). The ending -in (tanwīn kasra) marks it as indefinite ("a protector") and genitive — the "i"-type ending that appears after a preposition or in similar governed positions (often "of/from any protector").

19.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
19.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

20.meaning: "he associates / shares / makes a partner" — to take or set up someone as a partner alongside another, especially to ascribe partners to Allah; the core idea is making something a co-sharer.
20.grammar: A present/future verb of the causative pattern ("to make a partner of"). The prefix yu- marks the doer as "he" (with the "u" vowel signaling the causative fourth pattern). The final -u (ḍamma) is the indicative mood, marking a plain, ongoing/factual statement ("he associates"), as opposed to a commanded or hoped-for action.

21.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
21.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

22.meaning: "His ruling / judgement / authority / command" — the act or right of deciding, governing, and giving binding verdicts; wise governance and the decree that issues from it — here possessed by "Him."
22.grammar: A verbal noun ("ruling, judgement"). The base vowel -i is the genitive case, here showing the word is governed (e.g., after a preposition or in a possessive link). The attached -hi means "his / its"; its vowel is i (matching the preceding -i ending), and the long ī in recitation reflects the connecting pronoun.

23.meaning: Anyone / a single one: 'one' used to mean a sole individual, especially in negative or conditional contexts ('not anyone', 'any single person').
23.grammar: A noun meaning 'one / a single one', frequently used for 'anyone' when paired with a negation. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case typically used for a verb's object.

1.meaning: 'And recite / and read aloud / and follow closely'. A command to recite or read out something, with an underlying sense of following it along, word by word. The front particle adds 'and'.
1.grammar: An imperative (command) to one male: 'recite'. The final long -u is the natural ending of this command from a verb whose root ends in a weak letter. Prefixed wa- means 'and'.
1.root: ت-ل-و (t-l-w) — to recite, read out, follow

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: It has been revealed / inspired — divine communication has been sent down or conveyed (to someone). A passive verb: the focus is on the message being given, with the Giver understood rather than named.
3.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) passive verb (form IV). The opening vowelling marks it as passive ('it was/has been done to it'), and the ending denotes a third-person masculine singular subject — the thing revealed. Being passive, the doer (the Revealer) is left unstated. The long u of the prefix is formed by the damma plus the waw; the bare stem consonant carries -hi-.
3.root: و-ح-ى (w-h-y) — revelation, divine inspiration, conveying a message

4.meaning: 'To you' (addressing one person): indicating direction or motion toward a single individual — that toward which something moves or is directed.
4.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, towards') with an attached pronoun; before a suffix ilā takes the form ilay-. The -ka ending is the pronoun 'you' for a single male addressee. Pronouns following a preposition stand in the genitive relationship, though their form does not visibly change for case.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: "book / scripture / writing" — that which is written: a written record, document, or revealed Scripture; a prescribed or decreed writing.
6.grammar: A verbal noun of the fiʿāl pattern (kasra on the first syllable: ki-tāb), denoting "a thing written." The ending -i (kasra) marks the genitive case — the "i"-type ending typically appearing after a preposition or when one noun is possessed by/linked to another ("… of the Book").

7.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
7.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

8.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
8.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

9.meaning: A noun/participle meaning 'one who changes / alters / replaces.' It names the doer of changing — a substituter who exchanges one thing for another.

parts.en: one who … (prefix forming an active doer-noun)

9.grammar: An active participle (a doer-noun) from the intensive pattern, with the mu- prefix that marks 'the one who does' the action. The final -a is the accusative case ending, the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or after certain particles (such as 'there is no …').
9.root: ب-د-ل (b-d-l) — to change, exchange, replace

10.meaning: "for/to His words" — the spoken utterances, statements, or decrees; the plural of "word," denoting Allah's pronouncements or decisive sayings, here possessed by "Him."
10.grammar: The prefix li- is a preposition ("to/for"). The noun is a sound feminine plural marked by -āt ("words"). Its ending -i (kasra) is the genitive case, regular for the -āt plural and required after the preposition. The attached -hi means "his/its"; its i-vowel harmonizes with the preceding -i.
10.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — speech, word, utterance

11.meaning: A two-part expression combining 'and' with the particle of emphatic future negation. The core particle 'lan' negates a coming action with finality: 'will never / shall not (ever).' It denies that something will happen in the future, often with a tone of absolute impossibility.
11.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' ('and') joined to the negating particle 'lan'. 'Lan' governs a following present-tense verb, putting it into the subjunctive mood and turning its meaning into an emphatic denial of the future: 'it will never happen.'

12.meaning: A second-person present verb: 'you find / you come upon.' It denotes discovering or encountering something, whether by searching or by chance.
12.grammar: The ta- prefix marks a second-person masculine singular subject ('you'). The final -a vowel is the subjunctive, the shape used after governing particles (such as 'never' or 'that'), often projecting the action into the future.
12.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, to come upon

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
13.root: — (preposition)

14.meaning: Other than Him / apart from Him / besides Him. A relational word expressing the idea of being below, short of, or to the exclusion of something or someone.

parts.en: other than, apart from, besides, below

14.grammar: A relational noun/quasi-preposition meaning 'apart from / instead of'. It is followed by a possessive pronoun -hi ('Him'), which puts it in the genitive 'of' relationship; the kasra written under the pronoun reflects this genitive linkage.

15.meaning: "a place of refuge / shelter / asylum" — a spot one turns aside to for protection; a sanctuary or recourse where one takes cover.
15.grammar: A noun of place from the eighth (reflexive) pattern ("a place to which one turns for shelter"). The ending -an (tanwīn fatḥa) marks it as indefinite ("a refuge") and accusative — an "a"-type ending that commonly signals the object of a verb or a similar non-subject role; the written alif carries the tanwīn.
15.root: ل-ح-د (l-ḥ-d) — turning aside, inclining

1.meaning: And be patient / endure steadfastly / persevere — sabr is the disciplined restraint of the self: bearing hardship calmly, holding firm, and not giving way to impatience or despair. The leading wa is the connective 'and.'
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person, 'be patient!', carrying the connective wa ('and'). The clipped, vowel-less ending is the normal shape of the singular command form.
1.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, endure, restrain oneself, persevere

2.meaning: Your self / your own person. The 'self' or soul of a single person addressed as 'you', referring to one's own being.
2.grammar: A noun 'self/soul' with the attached possessive pronoun 'ka' ('your', addressing one male). The '-a' case-vowel before the pronoun is the accusative, which typically marks a direct object or something governed in that role.
2.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath, the inner person

3.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
3.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: 'They call / invite / summon' — to call upon, invite, or summon (also to pray to or call out to); a present-tense verb with a masculine-plural subject.
5.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they call/invite'). The ya- prefix with the full -ūna ending marks 'they (men) do' and shows the indicative mood — the plain statement form ('they do'), with its final nūn intact (contrast the jussive/subjunctive, where it drops).
5.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, summon, invite, pray

6.meaning: Their Lord, Master, and Sustainer — 'rabb' is the one who owns, nurtures, and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached pronoun, the Lord who is theirs.
6.grammar: A masculine noun with the possessive 'their' attached. The -a vowel before -hum marks the accusative case, the case typically used for the object of a verb.

7.meaning: In the early part of the day — the morning, the time of daybreak and forenoon.
7.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition ('in/at'), and al- is the definite article ('the'). The noun ends in tāʾ marbūṭa, which is pronounced as -t- when an ending follows; the final -i on it is the genitive ending, regularly taken by a noun after a preposition. Hence the inflected form is read 'ghadati'.
7.root: غ-د-و (gh-d-w) — morning, early part of the day

8.meaning: The latter part of the day — the evening, late afternoon into nightfall.
8.grammar: The wa- prefix is the conjunction 'and'; al- is the definite article 'the'. The final -i is the genitive ending, taken because the word continues the case of a preceding preposition or stands in a genitive construction.

9.meaning: they want / they intend — to will, desire, or purpose something. The verb conveys an active, ongoing intention or wish on the part of a group.
9.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (arāda, 'to will/intend'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural plus the indicative mood (a plain statement: 'they want'). The -na would drop under a particle that changes the mood.
9.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, will, intend

10.meaning: His face; the front of the head — and by extension one's whole self, presence, or the direction in which one turns. 'Surrendering one's face' idiomatically means devoting one's entire being.
10.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -hu meaning 'his.' The -a on the stem is the accusative ending, the case typically used for the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). With the pronoun it means 'his face/self.'
10.root: و-ج-ه (w-j-h) — face, direction, aspect; what one turns toward

11.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
11.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

12.meaning: "(it/you) goes beyond / overshoots / transgresses" — to pass over or move past something, to overstep a limit or boundary.
12.grammar: A present/future verb with a weak (defective) final root letter. The prefix ta- marks the subject as "you" (masculine singular) or "it/she" (feminine singular). The form is jussive: in the jussive of such defective verbs the weak final letter (the wāw) is dropped, and the -u (ḍamma) left on the dāl is the trace of that elision — it is a feature of the jussive defective verb, not an indicative ending.
12.root: ع-د-و (ʿ-d-w) — passing beyond, overstepping, enmity

13.meaning: "your two eyes" — the pair of eyes, the organs of sight, belonging to "you."
13.grammar: A dual noun: the -ā marks exactly two ("two eyes") in the nominative case — the form typically used for the subject of a sentence. (The dual's final nūn drops because a possessor pronoun is attached.) The suffix -ka means "your" addressed to a single male.
13.root: ع-ي-ن (ʿ-y-n) — eye, spring, source

14.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
14.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.

15.meaning: "you want / wish / intend / desire" — to seek after something, to will or aim for it, to have the purpose of obtaining it.
15.grammar: A present/future verb of the causative fourth pattern ("to seek/will"). The prefix tu- (with "u" vowel for this pattern) marks the subject as "you" (masculine singular) or "it/she" (feminine singular). The final -u (ḍamma) is the indicative mood, marking a plain, ongoing/factual statement ("you want").
15.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — seeking, willing, going to and fro

16.meaning: Adornment, beauty, finery — that which decorates and makes something attractive, whether ornament, fine clothing, or pleasing splendour.
16.grammar: A feminine noun. The final '-a' is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as a direct object or when otherwise governed into that state; the 't' here is the feminine marker pronounced in connected reading.
16.root: ز-ي-ن (z-y-n) — to adorn, beautify, decorate

17.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
17.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.
17.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, being alive, living

18.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
18.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
18.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

19.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
19.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

20.meaning: You obey, you comply with and submit to (someone's command); from a verb meaning to yield obedience.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form IV) in the jussive/apocopate mood. The tu- prefix marks 'you' (masculine singular). The bare ending (-ʿ with no final vowel) is the jussive form, used after particles like 'if' or negation/command particles, signalling a conditioned or non-indicative sense.

21.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
21.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

22.meaning: "We made (someone) heedless / We caused (him) to neglect" — the causative "to render unmindful, inattentive, or forgetful of something," the action ascribed to "We."
22.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb of the causative fourth pattern ("to make heedless"). The suffix -nā marks the doer as "we" and signals completed action — "We made (him) heedless." The opening alif (a-) belongs to the causative pattern and is fixed.

23.meaning: "his heart" — the heart as the inner seat of understanding, feeling, intention, and faith; belonging to "him."
23.grammar: A noun. The base ending -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case — typically the object of a verb ("… his heart" as what is acted upon). The attached -hu means "his/its"; its u-vowel follows the -a ending (and lengthens to ū in recitation as the connecting pronoun).
23.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart, turning over, inner core

24.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

24.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

25.meaning: "Our remembrance / mention / reminder" — the act of calling to mind, mentioning, or being mindful; remembrance and invocation, here belonging to "Us."
25.grammar: A verbal noun ("remembrance, mention"). The ending -i (kasra) marks the genitive case — the "i"-type ending appearing after a preposition or when the noun is possessed/linked ("… of Our remembrance"). The attached -nā means "our."

26.meaning: And he followed / pursued — to follow closely, comply with, and take as one's guide or path, with deliberate adherence.
26.grammar: A past-tense verb in the form VIII pattern, which intensifies 'to follow' into following closely and submitting to. Prefixed with 'wa-' ('and') and bearing no subject ending, the bare form takes a third-person masculine singular subject ('he').
26.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, to pursue, to comply with

27.meaning: His desire / his craving — the pull of one's lower self toward what it wants; whim, passion, or inclination, especially when it leads away from truth.
27.grammar: A noun ('desire, whim') with an attached third-person masculine singular possessive pronoun '-hu' ('his'), showing that the desire belongs to him. The word ends in a long final vowel (ā) and does not take a visible case mark, so its case is shown only by context.
27.root: ه-و-ي (h-w-y) — to incline, to fall; inclination, desire, whim

28.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
28.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

29.meaning: His matter, affair, command, or concern — the noun 'amr' covers a directive/command as well as a state of affairs or business; with the attached pronoun it means 'his affair' or 'his command'.
29.grammar: A masculine noun carrying the -u (nominative) ending, which generally marks the word as a subject or the thing being described/named. The attached -hu means 'his' or 'its', showing possession.
29.root: ء-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, to order; matter/affair

30.meaning: Something carried to excess, neglected, or let slip beyond proper bounds — an act done in a heedless, transgressing, or wasteful manner.
30.grammar: The -an ending is the accusative with nunation (tanwīn), marking an indefinite noun ('a/some...'); it commonly functions as an object or, as here, describes the manner or state in which something is done.
30.root: ف-ر-ط (f-r-ṭ) — to exceed, neglect, let slip; excess

1.meaning: "And say" — a command addressed to one male to speak or proclaim words.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb directed at a single male ("you"). The base imperative is qul; the final -i here is a helping vowel added only to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster — it is not a case or tense ending.

2.meaning: 'The truth / the reality; what is right, real, and rightfully due.' A weighty noun meaning that which is firmly true and real, as opposed to falsehood; it also carries the senses of a rightful claim, a duty owed, and justice. With the article it denotes 'the Truth' in a definite, absolute sense.
2.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- ('the') plus the stem. The final -u ending is the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word identifying what something is (as in 'X is the truth').
2.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, reality, rightness; that which is established and rightfully due

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

4.meaning: 'Your Lord' (Lord of a group) — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer who owns, governs, and gradually brings to fullness those He addresses.
4.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Master') carries an -i vowel before the attached pronoun, reflecting a genitive/possessive link. The ending -kum is the possessive pronoun for a group ('your', masculine/mixed plural), so together: 'the Lord belonging to you all'.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

5.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
5.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

6.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
6.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

7.meaning: An instruction meaning 'then let him believe' — a command directed at a third person, combining a connector with a verb of believing/having faith.
7.grammar: Built from fa- ('then/so'), the prefixed laam of command (giving the sense 'let him...'), and a present-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he'). The verb takes the jussive form with a final silent ending (sukūn on the final consonant), the mood used after the command laam.
7.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust; faith/belief

8.meaning: 'And who / and whoever' — the connective 'and' joined to the word 'man', which can be a question word ('who?') or a conditional/relative pronoun ('whoever, the one who').
8.grammar: A particle compound: the prefix wa- means 'and' (joining what follows to what precedes). 'Man' is an indeclinable pronoun used either to ask 'who?' or to mean 'whoever / the one who', commonly introducing a condition or a relative clause. It does not change its ending.

9.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
9.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.
9.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — to will, wish

10.meaning: An instruction meaning 'then let him disbelieve' — a command directed at a third person to reject faith or be ungrateful, combining a connector with a verb of disbelief.
10.grammar: Built from fa- ('then/so'), the prefixed laam of command ('let him...'), and a present-tense verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he'). The verb is in the jussive form with a final silent ending (sukūn), the mood required after the command laam.
10.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to disbelieve, to be ungrateful

11.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
11.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

12.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we made ready / we prepared in advance,' conveying the deliberate arranging or setting-up of something beforehand so that it stands ready.

parts.en: (part of the stem; the verb is from the form-IV pattern aʿtada)

12.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action verb. The attached -nā ending is the 'we' subject marker, telling you the doers are first-person plural. As a past-tense form it presents the action as already finished and accomplished.
12.root: ع-ت-د (ʿ-t-d) — readiness, preparing/making something ready

13.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'for/to the wrongdoers' — al-ẓālimūn being those who do wrong or injustice, who put things out of their rightful place; in religious usage especially those who wrong their own souls through disbelief or transgression.
13.grammar: A definite active participle (a 'doer' noun, 'those who wrong') in the masculine plural, governed by the preposition li- ('for, to'). The plural ending -īna is the genitive/accusative plural form, required here after the preposition. The single written lām after li- is the definite article 'the', its own letter merged into the preposition.
13.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to do wrong, oppress; injustice

14.meaning: Fire — blazing flame; by extension heat, burning, or (in many contexts) the Fire of punishment. The core image is leaping, consuming flame.
14.grammar: A feminine noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (the 'nunation' tanwīn). This ending commonly signals 'a fire' as the direct object of a verb, i.e. the thing acted upon.
14.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — to give light, shine, illuminate (نَار 'fire' is a derived noun from this root)

15.meaning: He encompassed, surrounded, or enclosed completely — to take in fully on every side, whether physically surrounding something or having total knowledge/grasp of it.
15.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in the third-person masculine singular ('he'). It is a Form IV verb (the pattern aFʿaLa, marked by the prefixed hamza 'a-'), which typically makes a root transitive or causative — here, to bring something wholly within one's encompassing. The final -a is the standard vowel closing a past-tense verb of this person.
15.root: ح-و-ط (ḥ-w-ṭ) — to surround, encompass, guard

16.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
16.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

17.meaning: Its enclosing wall, canopy, or pavilion — 'surādiq' is a surrounding screen or marquee that hems something in on all sides; with the attached pronoun it means 'its enclosure/walls'.
17.grammar: A noun bearing the -u (nominative) ending, which generally marks it as a subject. The attached -hā means 'its' or 'her', referring back to a feminine or non-human antecedent.
17.root: — (of Persian origin; no Arabic triliteral root)

18.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
18.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

19.meaning: They cry out for help, plead for aid or relief in distress — the verb expresses calling urgently for rescue.
19.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). It is a 'seeking' (Form X) verb, whose pattern conveys asking for or seeking out the action — here, seeking help. The -ū ending marks the masculine plural subject; the final form (without a fixed -na) reflects the subjunctive/jussive mood used after certain particles.
19.root: غ-و-ث (gh-w-th) — to help, rescue, bring relief

20.meaning: They are given relief, are aided, or are answered with help — the passive sense of being rescued or having one's plea for relief met.
20.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine plural ('they are helped'). The vowel pattern (yu- with a long ā) signals the passive voice — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The -ū ending marks the masculine plural; the final form (without fixed -na) reflects the subjunctive/jussive mood after certain particles.
20.root: غ-و-ث (gh-w-th) — to help, rescue, bring relief

21.meaning: With water — by means of water, the clear liquid essential to life.
21.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with / by means of'. Because it is a preposition, the following noun takes the genitive: the -in ending here is genitive with indefiniteness ('nunation'), so 'with (some) water'.

22.meaning: Like molten metal, dregs of oil, or molten copper/brass — 'muhl' denotes a thick, scalding molten substance; with the prefix it means 'like molten metal'.
22.grammar: A noun introduced by the preposition ka- ('like/as') and the definite article al- ('the'). The final -i is the genitive ending, the case regularly taken by a noun after a preposition (as in 'like the...').

23.meaning: It scorches, roasts, or scalds — the verb describes burning or searing something with fierce heat.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('it/he'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he/it' subject, and the present tense conveys an ongoing or habitual action. The final long -ī reflects the verb's weak (final-vowel) root.

24.meaning: The faces — 'wujūh' is the plural of 'face' (wajh), which can also mean countenance, presence, or direction; with the article, 'the faces'.
24.grammar: A definite plural noun (al- = 'the') taking the -a (accusative) ending, which typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

25.meaning: A fixed expression of strong blame meaning 'how evil/wretched it is!' or 'evil indeed is…'. It is a frozen verb of dispraise used to condemn whatever is mentioned after it.
25.grammar: A frozen verb of dispraise (its counterpart of praise is niʿma, 'how good'). It does not conjugate for tense; it introduces the thing being blamed and conveys 'what an evil … is …'.

26.meaning: The drink, beverage, or that which is drunk — 'sharāb' names a thing one drinks; with the article, 'the drink'.
26.grammar: A definite noun (al- = 'the') bearing the -u (nominative) ending, which generally marks the word as a subject or as the thing being identified in a statement.

27.meaning: 'And it became evil / how evil it is' — a past-tense verb of dispraise expressing that something is bad, wretched, or a wicked outcome. Used to condemn a thing as an evil example.
27.grammar: A third-person feminine singular past-tense verb ('it/she was evil'). The -at ending marks a feminine subject. As a verb of blame it functions like an exclamation of dispraise ('how evil … is!'). The wa- prefix means 'and.'
27.root: س-و-ء (s-w-ʾ) — evil, badness, to be bad/wretched

28.meaning: A resting place, a place to lean on for comfort, or a couch/abode — a spot one resorts to for ease and support.
28.grammar: A noun of place (the pattern mur-ta-fa- denotes the place where an action happens — here, where one rests or leans). The -an ending is the accusative with nunation, marking an indefinite noun that here specifies in what respect something is described.
28.root: ر-ف-ق (r-f-q) — to be gentle, companionship; ease/support (elbow, rifq)

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
4.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

5.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
5.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
5.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

6.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
6.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

7.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
7.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

8.meaning: To let something go to waste, to cause it to be lost, neglected, or made fruitless. Said of a 'we' subject in the present: '[we] let go to waste / cause to be lost.'

parts.en: let go to waste / cause to be lost

8.grammar: A present-tense causative verb meaning 'cause to be lost, let go to waste, allow to perish.' The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The final -u ending signals the indicative mood — the form used for a plain statement of fact ('we [do] let go to waste').

9.meaning: Means 'reward, wage, recompense'. The word denotes the due return for work or conduct — payment, compensation, or the reward earned by deeds.
9.grammar: A noun in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending. The accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon, e.g. 'the reward' as what is given or not wasted) or the first term of a possessive pair when it is itself an object ('the reward of…').
9.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense

10.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
10.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.
10.root: — (pronoun)

11.meaning: A verb meaning 'he did good / acted well, excellently' — to do what is beautiful, fine, and right; also 'he was good (at something)'.
11.grammar: A Form IV (afʿala) past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular 'he'; the bare -a ending marks a completed action by 'he'. Form IV here gives the sense of doing/making good, acting with excellence.
11.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — goodness, beauty, excellence

12.meaning: A deed / an action — a thing done, a work or act performed. The word names the action itself, stated indefinitely ('a deed').
12.grammar: A noun, 'deed/work/action'. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a deed') and accusative in case — the form typically used for the object of a verb or to specify 'as/in respect of'.
12.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; a deed

1.meaning: 'those / those ones' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things at a distance ('those there').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those.' The -ka element adds the sense of pointing to something farther off (as opposed to 'these' near at hand). Being a fixed pronoun, it keeps one form regardless of case.

2.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

3.meaning: Gardens — lush, densely shaded enclosures whose foliage covers the ground; the plural of the word for a garden, used pre-eminently for the Gardens of Paradise.
3.grammar: A feminine sound plural of 'janna' (garden), formed with the '-āt' plural ending. The final '-u' is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun that simply names or identifies something ('… are gardens').
3.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — covering, concealing; lush garden whose growth covers the earth

4.meaning: Perpetual residence, lasting settlement — an abode of permanence and enduring stay; classically a proper name for the Gardens of eternal dwelling.
4.grammar: A verbal noun used as a name for a place of permanent dwelling. The ending -in is the genitive case with nunation (tanwīn): the -i vowel typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …') or follows a preposition, while the final -n signals that it is indefinite.

5.meaning: A verb 'it flows, runs, streams' — used of water and rivers moving along, and of things that run or course freely. It describes continuous, ongoing motion.
5.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular. The ta- prefix here marks a feminine 'it/she' subject. The verb describes an ongoing or habitual action: 'it flows / keeps flowing.'
5.root: ج-ر-ي (j-r-y) — to flow, run, stream

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: Beneath them / underneath them — the spatial 'under' joined to an attached 'them', indicating the place directly below a group of males.
7.grammar: An adverb of place ('under') in the genitive, bound to the attached pronoun 'them'. As a locational word it normally follows a preposition like 'from', taking the genitive '-i'; the pronoun's vowel appears as '-himu' for ease of joining to the next word.

8.meaning: 'The rivers / the streams' — the definite plural of a word for a flowing river or watercourse. It denotes large, running channels of water.
8.grammar: A definite plural noun ('the rivers'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the doer of the verb or the thing being described.

9.meaning: They are adorned, decorated, or made to wear ornaments — the passive sense of being beautified with jewelry.
9.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, third-person masculine plural ('they are adorned'). The yu- prefix with the intensive doubled middle letter signals a Form II passive (to have ornaments richly applied to one). The -awna ending marks the masculine plural in the indicative mood (a plain statement of ongoing/future fact).
9.root: ح-ل-ي (ḥ-l-y) — ornament, jewelry, to adorn

10.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
10.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
10.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

11.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
11.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
11.root: — (preposition)

12.meaning: Bracelets, armlets — 'asāwir' is the plural of 'siwār', the band worn around the wrist or arm.
