12.grammar: A plural noun of a special pattern (a 'diptote') that resists nunation; its -a ending serves as the accusative, typically marking it as the direct object (the thing received or acted upon). This plural shape ordinarily also stands in for the genitive without taking nunation.
12.root: س-و-ر (s-w-r) — bracelet, armlet; to enclose

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
13.root: — (preposition)

14.meaning: Gold — the precious yellow metal 'dhahab'.
14.grammar: An indefinite noun with the -in ending: the genitive case with nunation. This case commonly links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship (e.g. 'bracelets of gold') or follows a preposition.

15.meaning: And they wear, put on, or clothe themselves — the verb of donning garments, joined by 'and'.
15.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they wear'). The ya-...-ūna frame marks the masculine plural subject in the indicative mood, expressing a plain ongoing or future fact.
15.root: ل-ب-س (l-b-s) — to wear, clothe, cover

16.meaning: Garments, clothes, robes — 'thiyāb' is the plural of 'thawb', a piece of clothing.
16.grammar: An indefinite plural noun with the -an ending: the accusative with nunation, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).
16.root: ث-و-ب (th-w-b) — garment; (also 'to return')

17.meaning: Green — the plural adjective 'khuḍr' (greens), the broken plural of 'akhḍar' (green); describes plural things that are green or verdant.
17.grammar: A colour adjective in the broken-plural form khuḍr (plural of the singular akhḍar, 'green'). As a descriptive word it agrees with the noun it modifies; here it takes the -an ending, the accusative with nunation. Such broken plurals are ordinary triptotes and regularly take nunation (unlike the diptote singular akhḍar, which does not).
17.root: خ-ض-ر (kh-ḍ-r) — green, greenery, verdure

18.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
18.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

19.meaning: Fine silk — 'sundus' is delicate, thin silk brocade.
19.grammar: An indefinite noun with the -in ending: the genitive case with nunation. This case commonly indicates an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun (e.g. 'garments of fine silk') or follows a preposition.
19.root: — (of non-Arabic, likely Persian/Greek, origin; no Arabic triliteral root)

20.meaning: And heavy/thick brocade — 'istabraq' is rich silk woven with gold thread, joined by 'and'.
20.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to an indefinite noun bearing the -in ending: the genitive with nunation, indicating an 'of' relationship to a preceding noun or coordination with another genitive noun.
20.root: — (of Persian origin; no Arabic triliteral root)

21.meaning: Reclining, leaning back at ease, propped up in comfort — describing those who rest by leaning upon something.
21.grammar: An active participle (a doer-word, 'one who reclines') in the masculine plural with the -īna ending. This ending marks the sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive; as a participle it often describes the state or circumstance in which people are found ('reclining').
21.root: و-ك-ء (w-k-ʾ) — to lean on, recline, prop oneself

22.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
22.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

23.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
23.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
23.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

24.meaning: The adorned couches, raised thrones, or canopied seats — 'arāik' is the plural of 'arīkah', a decorated couch or seat set within a chamber.
24.grammar: A definite plural noun (al- = 'the') of a special pattern that does not take nunation; its -i ending is the genitive, the case regularly used after a preposition (such as 'upon the...') or in an 'of' relationship.

25.meaning: How excellent! How good! A fixed verb of praise used to declare that something is outstandingly good. It is not an ordinary action verb but a formula that lavishes commendation on whatever follows it.

parts.en: how excellent is / what a good

25.grammar: A frozen verb of praise. It does not inflect for ordinary tense; it stands at the head of a statement to commend the noun that comes after it as supremely good. The closing -a is part of its fixed form rather than a productive case ending.

26.meaning: The reward, recompense, or requital — 'thawāb' is the good returned to someone for their deeds; with the article, 'the reward'.
26.grammar: A definite noun (al- = 'the') bearing the -u (nominative) ending, which generally marks the word as a subject or as the thing being identified in a statement.

27.meaning: A verb meaning 'it became good/beautiful' or 'it was excellent' — expressing that something turned out fine, pleasing, or commendable. The wa- at the front is the connector 'and'.
27.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -at ending marks a third-person singular feminine subject ('she/it did'), used for feminine nouns or things treated as grammatically feminine. The stem-pattern (ḥasuna) is the type used for adjective-like states, so it means 'became/was good' rather than an action done to something.

28.meaning: A place of rest, support, or comfort — a spot where one leans, settles, and finds ease; a resting-place or abode.
28.grammar: A noun of place built on the muf'ta'al pattern (a place where the action happens). The -an ending is accusative with nunation (the doubled 'n' sound), the case used for objects of verbs and, very commonly, for a word giving specification — answering 'in what respect?' ('as a resting-place').

1.meaning: A command meaning 'strike' or 'set forth' — literally 'beat/hit', but very widely used in the sense of 'put forward, present, coin (an example),' or 'travel through (the land).' The wa- is the connector 'and'.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one male: 'you, do this!' The helping vowel 'i-' at the start makes the consonant cluster pronounceable, and the bare, vowelless ending (-b) is the standard form for a singular masculine command.
1.root: ض-ر-ب (ḍ-r-b) — to strike; by extension to set forth or travel

2.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

3.meaning: A likeness, comparison, parable, or illustrative example — a similitude held up so that an abstract truth can be grasped through a concrete picture.
3.grammar: A noun. The -an ending is accusative with nunation (the doubled 'n' sound), the case typically marking the direct object of a verb — the thing acted upon ('an example').

4.meaning: Two men — the dual ('exactly two') of the word for 'man,' an adult male human.
4.grammar: A dual noun, meaning precisely two. The -ayni ending is the dual form used when the word is an object or follows a preposition or another noun ('… of …'); the same pair as a subject would end in -āni.
4.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, foot, to go on foot

5.meaning: We made, rendered, set up, or appointed. A completed act of making or designating, done by a group or by a majestic 'We.'
5.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb with the attached subject ending -nā, meaning 'we' did the action. 'Jaʿala' carries senses from 'to make/create' to 'to render X into Y' or 'to appoint.'
5.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

6.meaning: 'For one of the two of them' — combining the preposition 'for/to,' the word 'one (of a pair/group),' and 'them two.'
6.grammar: Preposition + noun + attached pronoun. The preposition li- ('for/to') puts the following noun in the genitive, shown by the -i on aḥad(i). The suffix -himā is the dual possessive/object pronoun 'the two of them' (its 'hi' vowel harmonizes after the -i).

7.meaning: Two gardens — the dual ('exactly two') of 'garden,' a lush, enclosed, green place; the same word is used for the Garden of Paradise.
7.grammar: A dual noun, meaning precisely two. The -ayni ending is the dual form used when the word is an object or follows a preposition or another noun; the matching subject form would be -āni.
7.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal; hence a garden whose foliage conceals the ground

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: A noun meaning 'grapevines / grapes' — the plural of the grape-cluster, vines bearing grapes.
9.grammar: A plural noun (the broken plural of 'grape/vine'). The -in ending (tanwīn) marks it indefinite and genitive — the case used after a preposition or to link it to a preceding noun ('… of grapes').
9.root: ع-ن-ب (ʿ-n-b) — grape, grapevine

10.meaning: 'And We surrounded the two of them' — to encircle, fringe, or border something on its sides. The wa- is the connector 'and.'
10.grammar: Past-tense verb with two attached pronouns. The -nā right after the stem is the subject 'we (did),' and the final -humā is the dual object pronoun 'the two of them.' So the form packs subject + verb + object: 'we surrounded the two of them.'
10.root: ح-ف-ف (ḥ-f-f) — to surround, encircle, fringe

11.meaning: 'With date-palms' — the preposition 'with/by means of' attached to the collective noun for palm trees (especially the date-palm).
11.grammar: Preposition + noun. The preposition bi- ('with/by') forces the genitive case on its noun, shown by the -in ending (the 'i' vowel plus the nunation 'n'-sound that marks an indefinite noun, 'some palm-trees'). Nakhl is a collective noun — singular in form but referring to palms as a group.
11.root: ن-خ-ل (n-kh-l) — date-palm; also sifting

12.meaning: 'And We made / We placed / We appointed.' A verb of making, fashioning, or setting something into a state or position, here joined to the preceding words by 'and.' Its sense ranges from creating and forming to assigning a role or rendering something a certain way.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb with the attached subject ending -nā ('we'), marking a completed act done by a plural or majestic 'we.' The wa- prefix means 'and,' linking it to what precedes.
12.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, place, render, appoint

13.meaning: Between the two of them — the space or relation lying amid a pair.
13.grammar: An adverb of place, 'between,' fixed in the accusative as adverbs of place commonly are; the -a marks its adverbial function ('in the place that is between'). The attached -humā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them' (exactly two).
13.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction; that which lies between

14.meaning: Sown crops, cultivated plants, or standing grain — vegetation deliberately planted and grown.
14.grammar: A verbal noun used concretely. The -an ending is accusative with nunation (the doubled 'n' sound), the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb — the thing acted upon or produced.
14.root: ز-ر-ع (z-r-ʿ) — to sow, plant, cause to grow

1.meaning: 'Both' / 'each of the two' — a word used specifically for a pair, emphasizing that what is said applies to both members of a duo together. (It is the feminine counterpart of kilā.)
1.grammar: A dual quantifier ('both') used with feminine pairs. It is followed by a definite dual noun in the genitive ('both OF the two …') and itself behaves as a singular for agreement, so a verb describing it is usually third-person feminine singular.
1.root: — (no triliteral root; an inherent dual word)

2.meaning: 'The two gardens' — the definite, dual form of 'garden,' a lush enclosed green place.
2.grammar: Definite article + dual noun. The al- means 'the.' The -ayni ending is the dual form ('exactly two') used when the word is an object or follows a preposition or another noun; the matching subject form would be -āni.
2.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal; hence a leaf-covered garden

3.meaning: 'It brought forth / it gave (its produce)' — a verb meaning to come, and by extension to yield up or deliver (as a plant brings forth fruit).
3.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -at ending marks a third-person singular feminine subject ('she/it did'), used for feminine nouns or things treated as grammatically feminine. Built on a heightened (form-IV) pattern of the verb 'to come,' giving the sense 'caused to come / brought forth.'

4.meaning: Its produce, fruit, or harvest — that which is eaten from a plant or garden, here marked as belonging to it.
4.grammar: A noun followed by the attached pronoun '-hā' (its, for a feminine owner). The '-a' on the noun before the pronoun is the accusative ending, which typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
4.root: ا-ك-ل (ʾ-k-l) — to eat; produce, food, fruit

5.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
5.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

6.meaning: '(It does not) wrong / fall short' — a verb meaning to act unjustly, to oppress, or to give less than what is due; also to be dark.
6.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ta- prefix marks a third-person singular feminine subject ('she/it does …'). The vowelless ending (-m) is the form a present-tense verb takes after a negating or jussive particle (e.g. lam, 'did not'), giving a negated past-like sense, 'did not wrong.'

7.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'from him/it' — indicating origin or source, that something proceeds out of him/it.
7.grammar: The preposition min ('from') with the attached pronoun -hu ('him/it', third-person masculine singular). As the object of a preposition the pronoun stands in the genitive; the combination indicates source or origin.

8.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
8.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

9.meaning: 'And We caused to burst/gush forth' — a verb meaning to split open and make flow, as in causing water to come pouring out. The wa- is the connector 'and.'
9.grammar: Past-tense verb with attached subject. The -nā ending means 'we (did).' The doubled middle consonant (intensive, form-II pattern) adds force or abundance — 'made gush forth copiously' rather than a single gentle splitting.
9.root: ف-ج-ر (f-j-r) — to split open, burst forth, gush

10.meaning: 'Through the midst of the two of them' / 'amid them two' — the noun for the spaces or intervals within/between things, plus the dual pronoun 'them two.'

parts.en: in the midst / through the intervals

10.grammar: An adverb-like noun of place + attached pronoun. It functions to mean 'in the midst/in between.' The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative ending typical of such place/time words used adverbially. The suffix -humā is the dual pronoun 'the two of them.'
10.root: خ-ل-ل (kh-l-l) — gap, interval, that which is between

11.meaning: A river, stream, or watercourse — flowing water in a channel.
11.grammar: A noun. The -an ending is accusative with nunation (the doubled 'n' sound), the case that typically marks the direct object of a verb — the thing produced or acted upon ('a river').
11.root: ن-ه-ر (n-h-r) — to flow abundantly; a river (also daylight)

1.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.

2.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
2.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

3.meaning: Fruit, produce, or yield — what plants and trees bring forth; can also carry the sense of profit or gains.
3.grammar: A noun. The -un ending is nominative with nunation (the 'u' vowel plus the indefinite 'n'-sound), the case that typically marks the subject of a sentence or a word standing on its own ('fruit').
3.root: ث-م-ر (th-m-r) — fruit, to bear fruit, produce

4.meaning: 'Then he said / so he said' — the past-tense verb 'he said,' introduced by a connector meaning 'then / so,' marking what follows as the next or resulting step.
4.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'then / so,' linking this to what came before and often implying sequence or consequence. The verb is past-tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'); the final -a is the base vowel of the 3rd-person masculine singular past form, marking that a single masculine subject performed the action.

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'to his companion / for his companion,' where the companion is one who accompanies, befriends, or keeps company with someone (singular male owner).
5.grammar: A noun with a prefixed preposition and an attached possessive pronoun. The prefix li- means 'to/for.' 'Ṣāḥib' is an active participle used as a noun, 'companion.' The -i ending is genitive, required because the word follows the preposition li-. The attached -hi means 'his,' so the whole means 'to/for his companion.'
5.root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — companionship, accompanying, association

6.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
6.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

7.meaning: 'He is conversing with him / debating him' — a verb meaning to exchange talk back and forth, to discuss or argue with another, with an attached object 'him.'
7.grammar: Present/imperfect verb with attached object. The yu- prefix marks a third-person singular masculine subject ('he does …'). The base -u ending is the plain present-tense (indicative) marker for an ongoing/habitual action. The mutual (form-III) pattern adds the sense of doing the act back-and-forth with someone. The suffix -hu is the object 'him.'
7.root: ح-و-ر (ḥ-w-r) — to return/exchange in speech; dialogue

8.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
8.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

9.meaning: Means "more" or "most" — the comparative/superlative of "many/much," denoting the greater or greatest in number or quantity.
9.grammar: A comparative/superlative form on the afʿal pattern ("more/most"). The -u ending is nominative, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the doer of a verb.
9.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — abundance, being many or much

10.meaning: 'Than you' / 'from you' — the preposition meaning 'from, of, than' attached to the pronoun 'you' (one male).
10.grammar: Preposition + attached pronoun. Min means 'from/of' and is the standard word used after a comparative to mean 'than.' The suffix -ka is the second-person singular masculine pronoun 'you' (the -a vowel marks it as masculine; a female addressee would be -ki).
10.root: — (a particle/preposition; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: 'Wealth / property / possessions' — material goods, money, and assets that a person owns.
11.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn) marks the accusative case (the object of a verb or otherwise governed) together with the absence of 'the' ('wealth / some property'). 'māl' covers money, property, and possessions generally.
11.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property, to be wealthy

12.meaning: 'And mightier / more powerful' — a comparative or superlative ('more/most mighty, stronger, more honoured') from a root joining dignity, strength, and being hard to overcome. The wa- is the connector 'and.'
12.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the af'al pattern ('more/most …'). The -u ending is nominative, the case that typically marks a subject or a predicate describing the subject ('… is mightier'). As an af'al form it takes no nunation.
12.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, honour, being strong and hard to overcome

13.meaning: A band of people, a group of supporters, kinsmen, or followers — those who rally to a person; also a small body of men.
13.grammar: A noun. The -an ending is accusative with nunation (the doubled 'n' sound). After a comparative adjective, an accusative noun like this commonly specifies the respect in which the comparison holds — answering 'in what?' ('… in men/followers').
13.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — to go forth, rally; a troop/band

1.meaning: A verb meaning 'and he entered / went in' — to enter or go inside a place. It refers to a single male who completed the action.
1.grammar: A completed past-tense verb. The bare '-a' ending with no added pronoun marks a single male doer ('he'). The 'wa-' prefix simply connects it with 'and'.

2.meaning: 'His garden' — the word for a lush enclosed green place, with the attached possessive 'his.'
2.grammar: Noun + attached possessive pronoun. The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case typically marking the direct object of a verb. The suffix -hu means 'his / of him,' so the whole is 'his garden.'
2.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal; hence a leaf-covered garden

3.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
3.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

4.meaning: One who does wrong — an unjust person, a wrongdoer or oppressor who puts things out of their right place or gives less than is due.
4.grammar: An active participle ('the one doing the action') on the fā'il pattern, describing a doer of wrong. The -un ending is nominative with nunation (the 'u' vowel plus the indefinite 'n'-sound), the case that typically marks a subject or a predicate describing the subject ('… is a wrongdoer').

5.meaning: To/for himself; expressing benefit, harm, or possession directed back at a single male person. Built from the preposition 'to/for', the noun 'soul/self', and the pronoun 'his'.
5.grammar: The prefixed 'li' is a preposition meaning 'to/for', often marking benefit or harm. Because of it, the noun takes the '-i' genitive ending (the form required after a preposition). The attached '-hi' means 'his/himself', referring back to a single male.
5.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, inner being

6.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
6.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: I suppose, think, or reckon; to hold an opinion or surmise, often with a sense of supposition or conjecture rather than certain knowledge.
8.grammar: A present/future verb. The 'a-' prefix marks the first-person singular 'I'. The '-u' ending is the indicative mood, the default form used for an ongoing or plain statement ('I suppose').

9.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
9.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
9.root: — (particle; no root)

10.meaning: It will perish, vanish, or pass out of existence; to be annihilated or come to ruin.
10.grammar: A present/future verb. The 'ta-' prefix marks a third-person feminine ('it/she') or sometimes second-person 'you'. The '-a' ending is the subjunctive, the form used after certain particles (such as 'that' or 'never'), signalling a dependent or intended action rather than a plain fact.
10.root: ب-ي-د (b-y-d) — to perish, become extinct

11.meaning: Feminine singular demonstrative pronoun, 'this (one)' — pointing to a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
11.grammar: A demonstrative ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand, contrasting with the masculine 'hādhā.' Demonstratives in Arabic do not change for grammatical case; the form stays fixed whether subject, object, or after a preposition.
11.root: — (demonstrative pronoun; no triliteral root)

12.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
12.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.
12.root: ء-ب-د (ʾ-b-d) — endless duration, eternity, perpetuity

1.meaning: A compound: the connective 'and' joined to the particle mā. The particle mā is highly versatile — it can mean 'what / whatever' (introducing an indirect question or a relative clause, 'that which'), or it can function as a negation ('not'). Context determines which sense applies; the core idea is an open, unspecified 'what(ever)' or a flat denial.
1.grammar: Two indeclinable particles, so there is no case ending to mark. The wa- prefix is the simple connective 'and', linking what follows to what precedes. Mā itself does not change form: it serves either as an interrogative/relative ('what, that which') or as a negating word ('not').

2.meaning: I suppose, think, or reckon; to hold an opinion or surmise, often with a sense of supposition or conjecture rather than certain knowledge.
2.grammar: A present/future verb. The 'a-' prefix marks the first-person singular 'I'. The '-u' ending is the indicative mood, the default form used for an ongoing or plain statement ('I suppose').
2.root: ظ-ن-ن (ẓ-n-n) — to suppose, think, conjecture

3.meaning: A noun meaning 'the Hour' — most particularly the Last Hour, the appointed time of the world's end and the Resurrection; literally a portion of time, an hour, or a moment.
3.grammar: A definite noun with the article al- (its l assimilates into the following 'sun letter' s, hence the doubled s). The -a ending is the accusative case, the case typically taken by the direct object of a verb or by what follows certain particles.
3.root: س-و-ع (s-w-ʿ) — a span of time, an hour; the appointed Hour

4.meaning: Standing, established, or coming to pass; that which arises or occurs. As a feminine active participle it describes the one (feminine) who/which stands or comes about.
4.grammar: An active participle ('the one standing/occurring'), made feminine by the '-a(t)' ending. The final '-an' (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a …') and in the accusative case, the form used for objects or predicates of certain verbs.

5.meaning: And if indeed; a compound opening a strong conditional clause. It combines 'and', an emphatic particle that puts weight on what follows, and 'if', so the sense is 'and surely, if…'.
5.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. The 'wa' connects to what precedes; the 'la' adds emphasis (often paired with an emphatic answer later); 'in' introduces a hypothetical condition ('if').

6.meaning: I was returned or brought back; to be sent or turned back to a former place or state, expressed passively (the action done to the speaker).
6.grammar: A past-tense passive verb. The inner vowel pattern (u–i) marks it as passive ('was brought back', not 'brought back'). The attached '-tu' ending means the subject is 'I'.
6.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to return, send back, repel

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
7.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

8.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
8.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

9.meaning: I will most certainly find; to come upon, discover, or obtain — here stated with the strongest emphasis ('I shall surely, definitely find').
9.grammar: A present/future verb of certainty. The 'la-' prefix and the '-anna' (heavy nūn of emphasis) together form an oath-like double emphasis: 'I will absolutely find'. The 'a-' within marks the first-person 'I'.
9.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon, obtain

10.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
10.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.
10.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, beneficial, choice, excellence

11.meaning: From it / from her — marking the starting point or source out of which something comes, referring to a feminine or grammatically-feminine thing.
11.grammar: The preposition 'from/out of' attached to the pronoun -hā ('it/her'), which refers back to a feminine or grammatically-feminine noun. After a preposition this pronoun stands in the genitive (object) position, giving the sense 'from it' — the source or point of departure of an action.
11.root: — (particle/preposition)

12.meaning: A place or outcome of return; the spot to which, or the state into which, one turns back — figuratively a final destination or end-result.
12.grammar: A noun of place/state derived from a verb meaning 'to turn back'. The 'mu-…-a-' pattern forms such a noun. The final '-an' (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a …') and accusative, the case used for objects or specifying complements.
12.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn, overturn, turn back

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
2.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

3.meaning: His companion, associate, or fellow; one who accompanies or keeps company, with the possessive 'his'.
3.grammar: An active participle used as a noun ('companion'). The '-u' ending is the nominative case, typically marking the subject/doer. The attached '-hu' means 'his', and the form points to a single male companion.
3.root: ص-ح-ب (ṣ-ḥ-b) — to accompany, befriend, keep company

4.meaning: 'And He' — the connective 'and' joined to the standalone pronoun 'He' (a single masculine person or thing), often introducing a new clause about the same subject.
4.grammar: A connective particle plus an independent pronoun. The wa- prefix means 'and', joining clauses or words. 'Huwa' is the detached third-person masculine singular pronoun; it carries no case ending, its final -a being fixed.

5.meaning: 'He is conversing with him / debating him' — a verb meaning to exchange talk back and forth, to discuss or argue with another, with an attached object 'him.'
5.grammar: Present/imperfect verb with attached object. The yu- prefix marks a third-person singular masculine subject ('he does …'). The base -u ending is the plain present-tense (indicative) marker for an ongoing/habitual action. The mutual (form-III) pattern adds the sense of doing the act back-and-forth with someone. The suffix -hu is the object 'him.'
5.root: ح-و-ر (ḥ-w-r) — to return/exchange in speech; dialogue

6.meaning: Do you disbelieve? A pointed question combining the questioning particle with the verb 'to reject faith' — to cover over, deny, or be ungrateful toward the truth.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb opened by the interrogative 'a-' ('do/did…?'). The '-ta' ending marks the subject as 'you' (a single male). The root sense includes both denying faith and ingratitude.
6.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, reject faith, be ungrateful

7.meaning: A combination meaning 'with/for the one that' or 'in exchange for that which'. It fuses the preposition bi- (with, by, in exchange for) onto the masculine singular relative pronoun alladhī ('the one who/that'), introducing a clause that further identifies the referred-to thing.

parts.en: the one who/that (masc. sing. relative pronoun)

7.grammar: bi- is a preposition that always governs a genitive; alladhī is an indeclinable masculine singular relative pronoun whose form does not change for case. It points to a single masculine entity and requires a following clause to complete its sense ('the one that …').

8.meaning: He created you; to bring you into being, originate or shape you from nothing — with 'you' as the one created.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb. The bare stem with final '-a' carries the third-person 'he' as subject. The attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (a single male): 'He created you'.

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
9.root: — (preposition)

10.meaning: 'Dust / earth / soil.' The noun turāb denotes dust or dry earth — the fine soil of the ground.
10.grammar: A masculine noun. The -in ending marks it as indefinite ('dust / some dust') and in the genitive case — the form used after a preposition (e.g., 'from …') or when linked to a preceding noun.
10.root: ت-ر-ب (t-r-b) — dust, earth, soil

11.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
11.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

12.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
12.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
12.root: — (preposition)

13.meaning: A drop of fluid; a tiny quantity of sperm/seminal fluid — by extension the minute beginning from which a human is formed.
13.grammar: A feminine noun (the '-a(t)' is its feminine form). The final '-in' (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a …') and in the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
13.root: ن-ط-ف (n-ṭ-f) — to drip, trickle; a drop of fluid

14.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
14.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

15.meaning: He fashioned, proportioned, or perfected you; to shape something into balanced, complete, well-formed order — with 'you' as the one so formed.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb of the intensive pattern (doubled middle), implying careful, thorough shaping. The base form carries an implied third-person 'he' as subject; the attached '-ka' is the object 'you' (a single male): 'He fashioned you'.
15.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to make even, proportion, perfect

16.meaning: 'A man' — an adult male human being. The word denotes a man specifically as a male individual, often with a sense of full-grown manhood.
16.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks the indefinite accusative, typically the case of a direct object or of a predicate following certain particles.
16.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — manhood, the adult male; (also the foot/to go on foot)

1.meaning: But as for me; a contrastive expression 'but/however' fused with the pronoun 'I', used to set up a contrast or correction ('but I, for my part…'). It is a contraction of 'but' plus the standalone 'I'.
1.grammar: A contraction of the light particle 'lākin' ('but, however') with the independent pronoun 'anā' ('I'): the initial vowel of 'anā' is dropped and its alif merges onto 'lākin', giving 'lākinnā'. The final '-ā' is the remnant of that pronoun 'I', not a case ending or a suffix on the heavy 'lākinna'. It introduces a statement that contrasts with what came before.

2.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
2.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
4.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

5.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
5.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

6.meaning: I associate or set up as a partner; to make something a partner or equal to another — in religious sense, to ascribe partners alongside Allah.
6.grammar: A present/future verb of the causative pattern ('to make a partner of'). The 'u-' prefix marks the first-person singular 'I'. The '-u' ending is the indicative mood, the plain form for an ongoing statement ('I associate').
6.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, take as partner

7.meaning: With/in my Lord; the preposition 'with/by/in' joined to 'Lord' (Rabb — the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and nurtures) and the pronoun 'my'.
7.grammar: The prefixed 'bi' is a preposition ('with, in, by'), which forces the following noun into the genitive ('-i'). 'Rabb' denotes one who owns, sustains and nurtures. The attached '-ī' means 'my'. Used here for Allah, the term is rendered 'Lord'.

8.meaning: Anyone / a single one: 'one' used to mean a sole individual, especially in negative or conditional contexts ('not anyone', 'any single person').
8.grammar: A noun meaning 'one / a single one', frequently used for 'anyone' when paired with a negation. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case typically used for a verb's object.

1.meaning: "and were it not for / and if not for" — a compound particle introducing a hypothetical: it points to something whose existence prevents a stated consequence, i.e. 'had it not been for X, then Y would have happened'.

parts.en: were it not for / if not

1.grammar: A particle phrase, not a verb, so it carries no case or tense ending. It sets up a conditional that is contrary to fact, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('then certainly…'). The leading wa- is the connector 'and'.

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

3.meaning: You entered, went into, or came in; to pass into a place or state — with 'you' as the one entering.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The '-ta' ending marks the subject as 'you' (a single male): 'you entered'. The bare stem 'dakhal-' carries the basic act of entering.

4.meaning: Your garden; an enclosed, lush, tree-filled garden or orchard, with the possessive 'your'.
4.grammar: A feminine noun meaning a dense, shaded garden (the root sense is 'to cover/conceal' — its foliage hides the ground). The '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking a direct object. The attached '-ka' means 'your' (addressing a single male).

5.meaning: 'You said' — to have uttered or stated something; addressed to a single male in the completed past.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix '-ta' marks a completed action done by 'you' (masculine singular): 'you said'.
5.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

6.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
6.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

7.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
7.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

10.meaning: Power, strength, might, or capacity; firmness and force, whether physical, military, or moral.
10.grammar: A feminine abstract noun ('strength, power'), marked feminine by '-a(t)'. The final '-a' is the accusative case, the form used for a direct object or after certain particles.
10.root: ق-و-ي (q-w-y) — to be strong, powerful, firm

11.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
11.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
12.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
12.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

13.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
13.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

14.meaning: You see me, regard me, or consider me (as something); to perceive with the eye or to deem/judge — with 'me' as the one seen.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb of seeing/regarding. The 'ta-' prefix marks the second-person 'you' (singular). The attached '-ni' (with its protective 'n') is the object 'me': 'you see/regard me'.

15.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
15.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

16.meaning: Fewer, less, or lesser; the comparative/superlative form of 'little/few' — smaller in amount, number, or worth.
16.grammar: An 'af'al' comparative/superlative form ('fewer/least'). The 'a-' prefix builds the comparative. The '-a' ending here is the accusative case, the form used for an object or specifying complement.
16.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — to be little, few, scant

17.meaning: 'Than you' / 'from you' — the preposition meaning 'from, of, than' attached to the pronoun 'you' (one male).
17.grammar: Preposition + attached pronoun. Min means 'from/of' and is the standard word used after a comparative to mean 'than.' The suffix -ka is the second-person singular masculine pronoun 'you' (the -a vowel marks it as masculine; a female addressee would be -ki).
17.root: — (a particle/preposition; no triliteral root)

18.meaning: 'Wealth / property / possessions' — material goods, money, and assets that a person owns.
18.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-an' ending (tanwīn) marks the accusative case (the object of a verb or otherwise governed) together with the absence of 'the' ('wealth / some property'). 'māl' covers money, property, and possessions generally.
18.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property, to be wealthy

19.meaning: And offspring/child(ren); 'and' joined to a noun meaning what is begotten — a child, son, or progeny (the word can denote one or, collectively, many).
19.grammar: The 'wa' prefix means 'and', joining this to a previous item. The noun's final '-an' (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a …') and in the accusative case, used for objects or specifying complements.
19.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to beget, give birth; offspring

1.meaning: A semi-frozen verb of expectation meaning 'perhaps, it may well be that …' When used of Allah it conveys a definite hopeful prospect; in general it expresses hoped-for likelihood.
1.grammar: A 'verb of approximation' (fiʿl al-muqāraba) expressing hope or likelihood ('perhaps it may be that …'); it is defective and semi-frozen, lacking the full range of tense conjugation. The prefixed fa- is a connector meaning 'so' or 'then,' linking it to what precedes.
1.root: ع-س-ي (ʿ-s-y) — hoping, expecting, drawing near (a defective verb of expectation)

2.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
2.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: He gives me, grants me, or bestows upon me; to hand over or provide something — with 'me' as the recipient.
4.grammar: A present/future verb of the causative pattern ('to give/grant'). The 'yu-' prefix marks the third-person 'he'. The '-a' is the subjunctive ending (the form after particles like 'that' or 'perhaps'). The attached '-ni' is the object 'me': 'he gives me'.
4.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to give, bring

5.meaning: Good — that which is beneficial, virtuous, and excellent; goodness as a thing one can do or possess, and what is better or preferable.
5.grammar: A noun (also serving as the 'better/best' form). The final -an (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case — the case used for the direct object of a verb ('to do good') and for similar governed roles.
5.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, beneficial, choice, excellence

6.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
6.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

7.meaning: Your garden; an enclosed, lush, tree-filled garden or orchard, with the possessive 'your', in the linking/genitive form.
7.grammar: A feminine noun for a dense, shaded garden. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition or when the noun is linked to a preceding word ('… of …'). The attached '-ka' means 'your' (addressing a single male).

8.meaning: And He sends / dispatches; the verb conveys releasing or letting something loose so that it goes forth — commonly used of sending messengers, but also of loosing rain, wind, or other forces.
8.grammar: Form IV (causative) imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final -a ending is the subjunctive (manṣūb) mood, which a verb takes after particles meaning 'that', 'so that', or 'in order to' — it signals a purposed or hypothetical action rather than a plain statement of fact.
8.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send, to dispatch; a messenger

9.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
9.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

10.meaning: A reckoning, computation, or fixed measured course — an arrangement by precise calculation. It conveys things moving according to an exact, ordained timetable.
10.grammar: An indefinite verbal noun with the '-an' ending (tanwīn), marking the accusative case. This ending commonly signals an object of a verb or expresses purpose/manner ('according to a reckoning'). The indefiniteness gives 'a reckoning'.
10.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — counting, reckoning

11.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
11.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

12.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
12.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
12.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; sky, heaven

13.meaning: Then it becomes / comes to be; a verb of 'becoming' that marks a transition into a new state. It originally meant 'to enter upon morning', and by extension came to mean simply 'to become' or 'to end up' in some condition.
13.grammar: Form IV imperfect verb, third-person feminine singular ('she/it') or second-person masculine singular ('you'). The final -a ending is the subjunctive (manṣūb) mood, taken after particles like 'so that' or 'then', expressing a consequence or purposed outcome rather than a bare fact.
13.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning; to come to be in the morning, to become

14.meaning: The surface of the earth; clean ground, dust, or fine soil — the upper face of the land.
14.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending (tanwīn 'a') marks the accusative case with indefiniteness ('some ground'). The accusative is the case of a direct object or of a noun governed by certain verbs and particles.
14.root: ص-ع-د (ṣ-ʿ-d) — to rise / ascend; the surface that rises uppermost

15.meaning: Slippery, smooth ground on which the foot finds no grip; bare, slick earth swept clean of vegetation so that one slides on it.
15.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative (manṣūb), marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). This ending typically marks the object of a verb, or — as often with such words — the predicate ('it becomes ___') or an adverbial sense describing how or into what something turns.
15.root: ز-ل-ق (z-l-q) — to slip, to slide; slipperiness

1.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
1.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

2.meaning: It becomes / comes to be; a verb of transition into a new state, originally tied to entering the morning, then generalized to 'to become' or 'to end up' in some condition.
2.grammar: Form IV imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final -a ending is the subjunctive (manṣūb) mood, taken after particles such as 'that' or 'so that', expressing a hypothetical or purposed outcome rather than a flat statement.
2.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning; to come to be in the morning, to become

3.meaning: Its water — the water belonging to it; 'water' as a substance, joined to a possessive pronoun referring back to some thing already mentioned.
3.grammar: A noun followed by the attached possessive pronoun -hā ('its/her', feminine singular). The -u vowel before the pronoun is the nominative (marfūʿ) case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the one doing or being something.

4.meaning: Water that has sunk deep into the earth and vanished beyond reach; a sinking-away or draining-down of water so that none remains at the surface.
4.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative (manṣūb), marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). This ending commonly marks the object of a verb or the predicate of a 'becoming' verb ('it becomes ___'), describing the state into which something passes.
4.root: غ-و-ر (gh-w-r) — to sink, to go deep down; a hollow, the bottom of something

5.meaning: So never / then never — a connector 'so/then' joined to an emphatic particle of negation that denies a future action absolutely: 'will never (at all)'.
5.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector meaning 'so/then', linking to what precedes. 'lan' negates a following present-tense verb and casts it into the future with emphatic force ('will never'); it also puts that verb into the subjunctive, which shows up as a final '-a' on the verb.
5.root: — (particle — no root)

6.meaning: You are able / you have the power to do something; a verb expressing capacity, capability, and having the means to accomplish a thing.
6.grammar: Form X imperfect verb, second-person masculine singular ('you'). The ta- prefix marks the 'you' subject; the final -a ending is the subjunctive (manṣūb) mood, taken after particles like 'that' or 'so that', expressing a potential or purposed action.
6.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, to be capable, to comply willingly

7.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
7.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

8.meaning: A seeking, a searching, a quest after something; the act of trying to find or obtain a thing, or the thing demanded itself.
8.grammar: A verbal noun in the indefinite accusative (manṣūb), marked by the -an ending (tanwīn). Here the ending often signals an adverbial or specifying sense — clarifying in what respect ('by way of seeking') — or marks the object of a verb.
8.root: ط-ل-ب (ṭ-l-b) — to seek, to search for, to demand

1.meaning: And it was encompassed / surrounded on every side; the passive of a verb meaning to wrap fully around, to hem in, and so to overwhelm and destroy completely — leaving no part untouched.
1.grammar: Form IV passive perfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('it was ___'). The internal vowel pattern (u–ī) marks it as passive — the action is done TO the subject by an unnamed agent. The final -a is the standard perfect (past) ending.
1.root: ح-و-ط (ḥ-w-ṭ) — to surround, to encompass, to enclose on all sides

2.meaning: With/by his fruit or produce — the yield of a tree or field, joined to a possessive pronoun; can also carry the wider sense of the gains and returns of one's wealth.
2.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/by') attached to a noun that carries the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('his/its'). The -i vowel is the genitive (majrūr) case, which a noun must take after a preposition.
2.root: ث-م-ر (th-m-r) — fruit, produce, yield

3.meaning: So he/it became / came to be / ended up — the verb 'to become' (originally 'to enter the morning'), here meaning to come into a new state. Introduced as a result ('and so he became...').
3.grammar: A past-tense verb introduced by fa- ('so/then') marking sequence or consequence. The bare stem with the -a vowel (-aṣbaḥa) is the past tense with a third-person masculine singular doer ('he/it became'). This verb of 'becoming' sets up a following description of the new state.
3.root: ص-ب-ح (ṣ-b-ḥ) — morning, daybreak; to come to be (by morning)

4.meaning: He turns something over and over, flips it back and forth; an intensive verb of repeatedly overturning — used both literally (turning a thing in the hands) and figuratively (wringing or clasping the hands in regret).
4.grammar: Form II imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it'). The doubled middle consonant gives an intensive or repeated sense ('keeps turning'). The final -u ending is the indicative (marfūʿ) mood, which marks a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('he does / is doing').
4.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn, to overturn, to flip; the heart

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'his two palms / his two hands' (specifically the palms or hollows of the hands). The dual form names a pair, and the attached pronoun marks them as belonging to 'him'.
5.grammar: A dual noun ('two palms') with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -ay- form is how the dual appears in the genitive/accusative (the object or 'of' form); the pronoun ending takes -hi rather than -hu because it follows the -i vowel of that dual ending.
5.root: ك-ف-ف (k-f-f) — palm of the hand, to restrain/hold

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on, upon, over, above', and by extension 'against' or 'incumbent upon'. It places one thing atop or as a duty/burden over another.
6.grammar: An indeclinable preposition (no case ending of its own). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun into the genitive case, and signals a relationship of being on top of, over, or binding upon something.

7.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
7.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

8.meaning: He spent, laid out, or expended (wealth); a verb of paying out money or resources, whether in a good cause or in waste.
8.grammar: Form IV perfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The a- prefix and pattern make it transitive ('to spend [something]'). The final -a is the standard perfect (past) ending, marking a completed action in the past.
8.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, to expend; to be used up

9.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
9.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
9.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

10.meaning: And she/it — a stand-alone subject pronoun for a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing or person, prefixed with 'and.'
10.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person feminine singular, 'she' or 'it.' Such pronouns stand alone as the subject or topic of a sentence and do not take case endings. The prefix wa- is the connective 'and.'

11.meaning: fallen down / collapsed / lying in ruins — a descriptive word for something caved in, empty and tumbled-down, fallen upon itself.

parts.en: fallen in ruins / empty and collapsed

11.grammar: An active descriptive noun (participle), feminine in form, describing a feminine thing as 'collapsed' or 'in ruins'. The final -un ending marks the nominative case (the subject or predicate role) together with the indefinite 'a/an', so it reads as a description: '(is) fallen in ruins'.
11.root: خ-و-ي (kh-w-y) — to be empty, to collapse, to lie in ruins

12.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
12.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

13.meaning: its roofs — the roofs or overhead structures of a thing, joined to a pronoun showing they belong to it (something feminine).
13.grammar: A plural noun ('roofs') with an attached possessive pronoun -hā ('its/her'), referring to a feminine owner. The -i vowel before the pronoun is genitive, the case used after prepositions or to show possession ('the roofs of it').
13.root: ع-ر-ش (ʿ-r-sh) — to roof over, build a structure; throne, canopy

14.meaning: And he says, and he will say. A verb of speaking covering plain statement, and by extension holding an opinion or asking.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb for a single male ('he says/will say'), joined by wa- ('and'). The ya- prefix marks the third-person masculine singular subject. The final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain statement of fact (ongoing or future) rather than a command or a 'so that' clause.

15.meaning: Oh, would that I…! / I dearly wish that I…; an exclamation of longing and regret, joining a cry of grief to a particle meaning 'if only', with 'I/me' attached — voicing a wish for what is contrary to fact.
15.grammar: An exclamatory particle yā ('O!') plus layta ('if only'), a particle expressing a wish for the impossible or improbable, with the attached pronoun -ī ('me/I'). When a first-person -ī pronoun attaches, a protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya) is inserted between the particle and the pronoun — giving -nī — to guard the particle's own final vowel (the fatḥa of layta) from being altered. The -nī here serves as the subject of the wish ('that I…').

16.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

16.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.
16.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

17.meaning: I associate / set up as a partner; a verb meaning to make something a partner or associate of another — most weightily, to associate anything with Allah in worship or sovereignty.
17.grammar: Form IV imperfect verb, first-person singular ('I'). The final consonant carries a sukūn (no vowel), marking the jussive (majzūm) mood — the form a verb takes after negative or conditional particles such as 'did not' or 'let', giving a negated or commanded sense rather than a plain statement.
17.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, to partner; to associate partners (with Allah)

18.meaning: With/in my Lord; the preposition 'with/by/in' joined to 'Lord' (Rabb — the Master who creates, owns, sustains, and nurtures) and the pronoun 'my'.
18.grammar: The prefixed 'bi' is a preposition ('with, in, by'), which forces the following noun into the genitive ('-i'). 'Rabb' denotes one who owns, sustains and nurtures. The attached '-ī' means 'my'. Used here for Allah, the term is rendered 'Lord'.

19.meaning: Anyone / a single one: 'one' used to mean a sole individual, especially in negative or conditional contexts ('not anyone', 'any single person').
19.grammar: A noun meaning 'one / a single one', frequently used for 'anyone' when paired with a negation. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case typically used for a verb's object.
19.root: ء-ح-د (ʾ-ḥ-d) — oneness, a single one

1.meaning: 'And not' — the conjunction wa- ('and') joined to lam, a particle that negates a verb and pushes its meaning into the completed past ('did not …').
1.grammar: A connector wa- ('and') plus the negative particle lam. Lam negates a following present-tense verb but turns its sense into the past: 'has not / did not …'. It also causes that verb to take the jussive (clipped) ending.

2.meaning: A short (jussive) form of the verb 'to be / to become', meaning 'be' or 'does not become / is not'. It expresses being, existing, or coming to be in a clipped form that typically follows a particle such as a negator or a command.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a second-person masculine singular ('you') or third-person feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The clipped final consonant (sukun, no vowel) is the jussive/apocopated mood, the form used after negative particles ('did not / was not') or as a command or prohibition.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

3.meaning: A two-part phrase 'for Him' or 'to Him belongs,' expressing possession, ownership, or that something is due to one masculine being.
3.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to/belonging to') with its vowel shifted to 'la-' before the pronoun. The attached -hu means 'Him', so the whole means 'for Him' or 'His'; the preposition signals possession or that something is owed or directed to that person.

4.meaning: A noun meaning a band, party, troop, or group of people — typically a body of people gathered together, often in a military or contending context.
4.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The closing -un (tanwīn / nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a group') and in the nominative case, the case typically used for the subject or doer of a sentence.
4.root: ف-ي-أ (f-y-ʾ) — returning / a group that returns or rallies together; فِئَة is a defective noun derived from this root and is sometimes treated as having a weak or dropped radical

5.meaning: They help / support / give victory to him; a verb of coming to someone's aid against an enemy, with 'him' as the one helped — joining the ideas of assistance and triumph.
5.grammar: A Form I imperfect verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), with the attached object pronoun -hu ('him'). The ya- prefix with the -ū- plural marker forms the masculine plural subject; the retained -na is the indicative (marfūʿ) ending, marking a plain statement of fact ('they help / are helping').
5.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to grant victory

6.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
6.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

7.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
7.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
7.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

8.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
8.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

9.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
9.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
9.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

10.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

10.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
10.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

11.meaning: One who defends or avenges himself; one who secures help, support, or victory for himself against another and so triumphs.
11.grammar: An active participle of Form VIII (a 'doer' noun: 'one who…'), masculine singular, in the indefinite accusative (manṣūb) marked by -an (tanwīn). The accusative here typically marks a state or circumstance ('being one who defends himself') or the object of a verb.
11.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, to aid, to grant victory

1.meaning: An adverb meaning 'there' or 'at that point' — pointing to a distant place, and by extension to a particular moment or set of circumstances ('right then and there').
1.grammar: A demonstrative adverb of place built from hunā ('there') plus the suffix -lika that signals farness, giving 'over there / yonder'. It is a fixed (indeclinable) word with no changing case ending, and can point to a time or situation as well as a place.

2.meaning: Protective guardianship; the bond of authority, alliance, and patronage by which one party protects, supports, and takes charge of another. It denotes both the right to protect and the close allegiance that comes with it.
2.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the') and the -u ending of the nominative (marfūʿ) case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence — the thing being spoken about or affirmed.
2.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near, to be an ally/guardian; protection, authority

3.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to', 'for', or 'belonging to', attached to the name 'Allah'. It conveys 'to Allah' or 'for Allah'.
3.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('to/for') pulls the following noun into the genitive case, which is why 'Allah' ends in '-i' (llāhi). The '-i' ending is the regular result of a noun governed by a preposition.

4.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
4.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
4.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

5.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
5.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').
