2.meaning: blocks / pieces / chunks — large solid lumps or masses of material.
2.grammar: A plural noun (singular zubra). The final -a (fatḥa) marks the object/accusative case — the form for the thing acted upon. As the first noun of a possessive pairing it links to a following noun ('blocks OF …').
2.root: ز-ب-ر (z-b-r) — a solid mass, lump, or piece

3.meaning: iron — the hard metal; the substance itself.
3.grammar: A noun with the attached al- ('the'). The final -i (kasra) is the genitive ending: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF iron') or follows a preposition.
3.root: ح-د-د (ḥ-d-d) — sharpness, hardness, a firm boundary; hence iron

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'until, up to the point that,' or 'so that.' It marks an end-limit in time, place, or purpose — the boundary at which something culminates or the goal toward which it moves.
4.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It introduces an end-point or goal; when followed by a verb it can express purpose or result ('until' / 'so that').

5.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
5.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: he made level / he brought even — to bring two things to the same height so they are flush and equal.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb on the III-form (sāwā, 'to make equal/level'). With no separate subject ending it carries a 'he' subject: 'he leveled / made even'. The final long -ā is the verb's own weak final letter, not a case ending.
6.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to be even, level, equal

7.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
7.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

8.meaning: the two cliff-sides / the two mountain faces — the two steep slopes or escarpments that face each other across a gap.
8.grammar: A noun with al- ('the') in the dual (exactly two). The -ayni ending marks the dual in the object or genitive case — 'the two cliff-faces' as the thing acted upon or linked to a preposition.
8.root: ص-د-ف (ṣ-d-f) — the side or steep face of a mountain

9.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
9.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
9.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

10.meaning: blow / puff — a command to drive air forcefully, as onto a fire to make it blaze.
10.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group, from the verb 'nafakha' (to blow). The -ū ending marks a plural command ('you all, blow!'); the written final alif after it is silent. The opening alif is a helping vowel to start the word.
10.root: ن-ف-خ (n-f-kh) — to blow, breathe out air

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'until, up to the point that,' or 'so that.' It marks an end-limit in time, place, or purpose — the boundary at which something culminates or the goal toward which it moves.
11.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It introduces an end-point or goal; when followed by a verb it can express purpose or result ('until' / 'so that').

12.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
12.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'he made it', 'he rendered it', or 'he turned it into something' — combining the act of making/causing by a single male with 'it' as what is acted upon.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb for a single masculine subject ('he made'), with the attached object pronoun '-hu' ('it / him'). The verb often takes two objects, conveying turning one thing into another ('he made it [into] …').
13.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, bring about

14.meaning: Fire — blazing flame; by extension heat, burning, or (in many contexts) the Fire of punishment. The core image is leaping, consuming flame.
14.grammar: A feminine noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the -an ending (the 'nunation' tanwīn). This ending commonly signals 'a fire' as the direct object of a verb, i.e. the thing acted upon.
14.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — to give light, shine, illuminate (نَار 'fire' is a derived noun from this root)

15.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
15.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.
15.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, uttering

16.meaning: bring me / give me — a command to fetch or hand over something to the speaker.
16.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group, from the IV-form verb 'ātā' (to bring, give). The -ū ending marks a plural command ('you all, bring!'), and the attached -ī is the object 'me'. The nūn before -ī is the protective nūn (nūn al-wiqāya) that supports the first-person object pronoun.
16.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; in the IV-form, to bring or give

17.meaning: I pour out / let me pour — to make a molten or liquid substance flow out over something.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb on the IV-form (afragha, 'to pour out') with the u- prefix meaning 'I'. The vowel-less final (jussive form, -∅) is the shortened mood used in answers to conditions or commands, giving 'I shall pour' / 'let me pour'.
17.root: ف-ر-غ (f-r-gh) — to empty out, pour out completely

18.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
18.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

19.meaning: molten metal / liquefied copper — metal melted by intense heat so that it flows and can be poured.
19.grammar: A noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite ('molten metal') and in the object/accusative case — the form for the thing acted upon.
19.root: ق-ط-ر (q-ṭ-r) — to drip, flow in drops; hence molten metal that pours

1.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
1.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

2.meaning: they were able / they had the power to — to possess the capacity or strength to do something.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb meaning 'to be able' (a lightened form of istaṭāʿa). The -ū ending marks the masculine plural subject 'they (did)'; the written final alif is silent. The opening alif is a helping vowel to start the word.
2.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, comply; in this form, to be capable/able

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: to climb over it / scale it / surmount it — to mount up the surface of something and pass over its top.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a 'they' (masculine plural) subject and the -ū plural ending. Because it follows a governing particle, the normal final nūn of '-ūna' has dropped, leaving '-ū'. The attached -hu is the object 'it': 'they scale it'.
4.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — to appear, become outward; to climb upon / get on top of

5.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
5.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
5.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

6.meaning: They were able / had the power / managed to — possessing the capacity to do something.
6.grammar: A past-tense verb on the 'seeking' (form X) pattern, here meaning 'to have the capacity / be able'. The -ū ending means 'they' (masculine plural) as the doers of a completed action. (The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention, not a sound.)

7.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
7.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

8.meaning: a hole / a bore / a breach — an opening made by digging or piercing through something.
8.grammar: A noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥ) marks it as indefinite ('a hole') and in the object/accusative case — the form for the thing acted upon.
8.root: ن-ق-ب (n-q-b) — to bore, pierce, dig through

1.meaning: 'He said' — to speak, utter, or declare; the basic verb for saying words aloud, from the root meaning speech and utterance.
1.grammar: Past tense. The base verb with a final -a marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and completed action ('he said'). The middle root letter (w) appears as a long -ā- inside this hollow verb.

2.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
2.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

3.meaning: a mercy — compassion that issues in real kindness, relief, and benefit; an act or gift flowing from such compassion.
3.grammar: A noun. The final -un (tanwīn ḍamm) marks it as indefinite ('a mercy') and in the subject (nominative) case — the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being identified.

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: 'My Lord' — the word 'rabb' denotes the Lord, Master, Sustainer and Nurturer who creates, owns, governs and brings a thing to its full development; with the attached 'my' it expresses one's own Lord and Caretaker.
5.grammar: A noun followed by the possessive ending '-ī' meaning 'my', which joins to the noun and also serves the genitive (possessive) relationship. The attached '-ī' both makes the noun definite and shows ownership: 'my Lord'.
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, nurturing, sustaining

6.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
6.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.

7.meaning: He/it came, arrived, or came about — the act of coming into presence or of something occurring.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb with no prefix and no personal suffix, naming a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it came'). All three letters here are root letters: jā spells the first radical plus the lengthened weak middle radical, and the final hamza (ء) is the third root consonant — not an ending. The fatḥa (-a) on that hamza is simply the past-tense vocalization for a 'he' subject sitting on the last root letter; there is no separable suffix.

8.meaning: The promise, pledge, or appointed assurance; a binding undertaking that something will come to pass — whether a good thing promised or a threatened outcome.
8.grammar: A verbal noun, 'a promise/pledge.' The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject; in a possessive phrase it also carries the 'X of Y' sense ('the promise of …'), the following noun completing it.
8.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — promising, pledging, an appointed assurance

9.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
9.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
9.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'he made it', 'he rendered it', or 'he turned it into something' — combining the act of making/causing by a single male with 'it' as what is acted upon.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb for a single masculine subject ('he made'), with the attached object pronoun '-hu' ('it / him'). The verb often takes two objects, conveying turning one thing into another ('he made it [into] …').
10.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, bring about

11.meaning: flattened / leveled to the ground — reduced to a low, even heap, crumbled flat so nothing stands above the rest.
11.grammar: An adjective on the 'faʿʿāʾ' pattern (with the doubled middle radical, here the geminated kāf) describing something made flat and even. Its final -a (fatḥa) shows the diptote ending: such words take -a (rather than -i) in the genitive/accusative and do not take indefinite tanwīn.
11.root: د-ك-ك (d-k-k) — to flatten, crush down, level to the ground

12.meaning: And he was / he became — a verb of being that places a subject in a past state or links it to a description in the past.
12.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'kāna' is a past-tense verb, 3rd-person masculine singular, meaning 'he was/became'; it commonly introduces a past condition and is typically followed by a noun describing the subject's state. The final -a marks completed past action by a single male.
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence

13.meaning: The promise, pledge, or appointed assurance; a binding undertaking that something will come to pass — whether a good thing promised or a threatened outcome.
13.grammar: A verbal noun, 'a promise/pledge.' The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject; in a possessive phrase it also carries the 'X of Y' sense ('the promise of …'), the following noun completing it.
13.root: و-ع-د (w-ʿ-d) — promising, pledging, an appointed assurance

14.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
14.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
14.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

15.meaning: A right, a due, or an obligation — that which is true, real, and rightfully owed; an established duty. As an adverbial accusative it conveys "as a duty/obligation, in truth, bindingly."
15.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with a following alif) often functions adverbially here — "as a binding duty" or "in truth" — describing the manner or affirming the statement.
15.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, right, established; truth, right

1.meaning: 'and we left / left behind / abandoned'. It denotes leaving something in place, departing from it, or setting it aside.
1.grammar: 'And' (wa-) joined to a past-tense verb. The attached -nā ending marks a 'we' (first-person plural) subject in completed past time ('and we left').

2.meaning: "some of them / a part of them" — the word baʿḍ means 'a portion/some', and with the attached pronoun it means 'some of them', singling out part of a group.
2.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive/partitive pronoun. The -a ending is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the object of an action or the second term of certain constructions. The suffix -hum means 'them' (third-person masculine plural).
2.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — part, portion, some

3.meaning: On that day / that day — pointing back to a particular past day already in view; 'a day, at that time.'
3.grammar: A time-word ('day') joined to 'idhin' ('at that time'), together meaning 'on that day.' The '-in' ('tanwīn') compensates for an understood clause ('the day when…'). The form functions adverbially, locating an event at a specific past moment.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'to surge, billow, heave in waves' — to move like the swelling, restless motion of the sea, with masses rolling and crashing into one another.

parts.en: he/it (3rd-person masculine subject prefix; the doubling reflects an assimilated 'wa-' joined before it)

4.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a single masculine 'he/it' as the doer, so the sense is 'he/it surges/billows'; the shadda (doubling) on the yāʾ comes from a preceding 'wa-' ('and') that has assimilated into it. The -u ending is the indicative mood, the plain form used for an ongoing or habitual action that is simply being stated.

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
6.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
6.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

7.meaning: 'And it was blown / will be blown' — a passive verb describing the act of blowing breath or air into something, as into a trumpet or horn.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice, where the doer is left unnamed and the focus falls on the action itself: 'it was blown'. The internal vowel pattern (u–i: nufikha) is the hallmark of the passive. The final -a is the standard ending of this past-tense form; the wa- prefix simply means 'and'.

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
8.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

9.meaning: The horn or trumpet — the great horn that is sounded; also the natural sense of a horn-shaped instrument blown to summon or signal.
9.grammar: Definite noun ('the trumpet'). The al- prefix means 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
9.root: ص-و-ر (ṣ-w-r) — form, shape; here a horn or trumpet

10.meaning: 'Then We gathered / will gather them' — to bring scattered people or things together into one assembled mass.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb. The attached -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers, and the attached -hum is the object 'them', so the whole reads 'we gathered them'. The fa- prefix means 'then/so', signalling a result or a next step.
10.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — gathering, joining together

11.meaning: 'A gathering / an assembling' — the verbal noun naming the act of bringing together, often used to intensify a related verb, conveying 'gathering them in one complete gathering'.
11.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action of gathering). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative; on such a noun it commonly works as an emphasising 'inner object' — reinforcing a matching verb in the sense 'to gather a thorough gathering'.
11.root: ج-م-ع (j-m-ʿ) — gathering, joining together

1.meaning: 'And We presented / displayed' — to bring something forward and set it out in plain view, to put it on display or parade it before onlookers.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The attached -nā ending marks 'we' as the doers, giving 'we presented/displayed'. The wa- prefix means 'and'.
1.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — presenting, displaying, setting before view

2.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
2.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
2.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

3.meaning: On that day / that day — pointing back to a particular past day already in view; 'a day, at that time.'
3.grammar: A time-word ('day') joined to 'idhin' ('at that time'), together meaning 'on that day.' The '-in' ('tanwīn') compensates for an understood clause ('the day when…'). The form functions adverbially, locating an event at a specific past moment.

4.meaning: For/to those who reject faith — the active participle 'kāfir' (one who covers over, conceals, and so denies the truth) in its sound masculine plural, preceded by the preposition 'li-' meaning 'to' or 'for'.
4.grammar: The 'li-' prefix means 'to/for'. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, used after a preposition; it marks 'the rejecters' as the object of 'for'. The base is an active participle: 'one who is rejecting/covering up faith'.
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, and thus reject or disbelieve

5.meaning: 'A presenting / a display' — the verbal noun naming the act of setting something out openly for view, often used to intensify a related verb ('to present in full display').
5.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the action of presenting). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative; on such a noun it typically serves as an emphasising 'inner object' that reinforces a matching verb, e.g. 'displayed it in a clear display'.
5.root: ع-ر-ض (ʿ-r-ḍ) — presenting, displaying, setting before view

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she was / it was / it became' — from the core verb of being, linking a subject to a description or state, often setting it in past or established time.
2.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb of being. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it was'. As a being-verb it normally introduces a description of that subject.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

3.meaning: 'Their eyes' — the plural of 'eye', the organ of sight; by extension it can also mean springs of water or one's very selves, though the core sense is the eyes.
3.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun with an attached possessive -hum meaning 'their'. The -u vowel before the suffix is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject — the one doing or being something.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: 'A cover / covering / veil' — anything spread over a thing to conceal or shroud it, a screen that blocks it from sight or perception.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -in ending (the 'n' sound, called nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a cover'), and the -i vowel it carries is the genitive case — the form used after a preposition or to link it to a preceding noun ('… of …').
5.root: غ-ط-و / غ-ط-ي (gh-ṭ-w/y) — covering, veiling, screening

6.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

6.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

7.meaning: 'My remembrance / My reminder' — the act of calling to mind, mentioning, and being mindful, tied to a possessor: remembrance OF me, or my mention of something.
7.grammar: A verbal noun with the attached possessive -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending fixes the word's case, so it reads simply 'my remembrance / my reminder'.
7.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — remembering, mentioning, calling to mind

8.meaning: A compound meaning 'and they were' or 'and they used to' — it sets a state or habit in the past. The verb 'to be/become' here establishes an ongoing past condition, often paired with a following verb to express habitual action.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb ('to be') in the third-person masculine plural — the -ū ending means 'they' did/were. It commonly conveys a continued past state or habit, especially when followed by another verb. The wa- prefix means 'and.'
8.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being

9.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

10.meaning: They are able / they have the power and capacity — to be capable of doing something, to have the strength, means, or ability to carry it out.
10.grammar: Present-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the present tense and the 'they' subject; the -ūna ending marks the plural and the indicative mood — the plain factual form for an ongoing state. From form X, which often carries the sense of 'seeking/having the capacity for' something, here simply 'to be able.'
10.root: ط-و-ع (ṭ-w-ʿ) — to obey, to be capable, willing capacity

11.meaning: 'Hearing / listening' — the verbal noun naming the faculty and act of perceiving sound with the ears, or attentive listening.
11.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the act of hearing). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed in that case.
11.root: س-م-ع (s-m-ʿ) — hearing, listening

1.meaning: An opening combination: 'Then does … reckon/suppose?' — built on the verb 'to reckon, suppose, think, count', framed as a pointed question expecting a 'no'.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb 'he reckoned/supposed' carrying a built-in 'he' subject (3rd-person masculine singular), with the final -a being its standard ending. The a- prefix turns the statement into a question, and fa- means 'then/so'; together they introduce a rhetorical challenge.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
4.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

5.meaning: Present/future verb (reflexive form), third person plural: 'they take for themselves, adopt, choose.' It denotes taking something on as one's own — selecting it and making it one's possession or position.
5.grammar: An ongoing/future verb in a reflexive pattern (taking something for oneself). The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person subject and the long '-ū' ending makes it 'they' (masculine plural). The prefix yā' here carries a shadda (doubling), which arises when a preceding word's final 'n' assimilates into it. The bare '-ū' (no final 'n') is the form used after particles meaning 'that they…' or in negative/command constructions.
5.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp

6.meaning: A phrase meaning 'my servants / my worshippers' — those who serve and worship, bound to a master, with 'my' marking them as belonging to the speaker.
6.grammar: A masculine plural noun, ʿibād ('servants, worshippers', plural of ʿabd), with the attached possessive pronoun -ī ('my'). Before this 'my' suffix the noun's case vowel is replaced by the -i linking sound, so the form reads ʿibādī, denoting 'my servants'.

7.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
7.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

8.meaning: Apart from Me / instead of Me / below Me — the word dūn marks something as other than, lesser than, or to the exclusion of a reference point; with the attached 'Me' it means 'taking others rather than, or in place of, Myself.'
8.grammar: A relational noun (functioning much like a preposition) meaning 'apart from / other than,' here in the genitive with the first-person possessive pronoun -ī ('me'). The -ī ending is the attached 'my/me' pronoun; dūn governs a following noun in the genitive, so the whole expresses exclusion or substitution: 'to the exclusion of Me.'
8.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — being lower, nearer, or short of something; hence 'other than / besides'

9.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
9.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).
9.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, allegiance, guardianship

10.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
10.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

11.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'we made ready / we prepared in advance,' conveying the deliberate arranging or setting-up of something beforehand so that it stands ready.

parts.en: (part of the stem; the verb is from the form-IV pattern aʿtada)

11.grammar: A completed (past-tense) action verb. The attached -nā ending is the 'we' subject marker, telling you the doers are first-person plural. As a past-tense form it presents the action as already finished and accomplished.
11.root: ع-ت-د (ʿ-t-d) — readiness, preparing/making something ready

12.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
12.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
12.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

13.meaning: A three-part word: 'for' + 'the' + 'those who cover up the truth / reject faith.' The base noun denotes the kāfir — one who disbelieves, denies, and ungratefully conceals the truth and Allah's favor. With 'for,' it marks them as the ones for whom something is intended.
13.grammar: The preposition 'li-' ('for/to') joined to a definite plural noun, masculine. The '-īna' ending is the sound masculine plural in its genitive/accusative (oblique) form, here required because it follows the preposition 'li-'. The whole denotes 'for the disbelievers.'
13.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

14.meaning: An offering of welcome, a lodging prepared for a guest, or a hospitable provision laid out on arrival.
14.grammar: A masculine noun, indefinite. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks the accusative, commonly used here for an object or in an explanatory sense ('as a welcome-gift').
14.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — descending, alighting, being a guest

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
2.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

3.meaning: 'We inform you / tell you of grave news' — to convey a weighty announcement or tidings; the doubled middle root letter gives the sense of fully and emphatically informing.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The nu- prefix marks 'we' as the doers, and the attached -kum is the object 'you (plural)', giving 'we inform you'. The -u mood-vowel before the suffix is the plain indicative, used for a simple statement of an ongoing or imminent action.

4.meaning: 'The greatest losers / those who lose the most' — those who incur the worst loss, whose venture ends in the deepest deficit and ruin.
4.grammar: A superlative noun ('the most loss-incurring') in the sound masculine plural, prefixed by 'the' and the preposition bi- ('of/about'). The -īna ending is that plural form in the genitive/accusative state, used because a preposition precedes it.

5.meaning: 'Deeds / works / actions' — the plural of 'deed', covering anything a person does or carries out, whether labour, conduct, or performance.
5.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative; on such a word it often answers 'in what respect?' — i.e. 'as to (their) deeds'.
5.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — doing, working, action

1.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
1.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

2.meaning: He strayed, lost the way, or went off course — to wander from the right path, whether literally or figuratively (to err, be misguided, or deviate from truth and guidance).
2.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he went astray'. The bare past-tense form with the -a ending signals a single male (or thing) as the doer of a completed action.
2.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to go astray, lose the way, err

3.meaning: 'Their effort / striving / endeavour' — the verbal noun for earnest exertion, running about in pursuit of a goal, and the labour one expends; joined to 'their'.
3.grammar: A verbal noun with an attached possessive -hum meaning 'their'. The -u vowel before the suffix is the nominative case, the form a noun takes as the subject — the thing being spoken about ('their effort').

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
5.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.
5.root: ح-ي-ي (ḥ-y-y) — life, being alive, living

6.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
6.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
6.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

7.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
7.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

8.meaning: 'They reckon / suppose / think' — to form an opinion or assume something to be the case; the verb also carries the sense of counting or calculating.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks 'they' (a masculine plural) as the doers: 'they reckon/suppose'. The retained -na is the sign of the plain indicative mood, used for a simple ongoing statement.

9.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
9.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

10.meaning: 'They do well / act rightly / produce good work' — to perform something excellently and beautifully, to do good and make a thing fine and proper.
10.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (the 'make/cause' pattern meaning 'to do something well'). Form IV is identified by its stem shape — a ḍamma on the imperfect prefix together with a kasra on the first root letter (yu-ḥsin-) — not by the prefix letter alone, since the y-/n- prefixes are the ordinary person markers shared by every verb form. The yu- prefix plus the -ūna ending marks 'they' (masculine plural) as the doers, and the retained -na shows the plain indicative mood for a simple statement.
10.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — goodness, beauty, doing well

11.meaning: 'Workmanship / making / craft' — the verbal noun for skilled production: how something is fashioned, crafted, or accomplished, the deed seen as a piece of work.
11.grammar: A verbal noun (the name of the act of crafting). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative; on such a word it commonly specifies 'in what respect?' — i.e. 'as to (their) workmanship'.
11.root: ص-ن-ع (ṣ-n-ʿ) — making, crafting, fashioning

1.meaning: 'those / those ones' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things at a distance ('those there').
1.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those.' The -ka element adds the sense of pointing to something farther off (as opposed to 'these' near at hand). Being a fixed pronoun, it keeps one form regardless of case.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
3.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

4.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
4.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
4.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

5.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the base 'rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer: the one who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to maturity. As a divine title it conveys Allah as Creator and Sustainer of all.
5.grammar: The noun 'rabb' ('Lord, Sustainer') with the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive case, the form used after a preposition or, as in a possessive linkage, to show belonging ('of/their').
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, master, sustain; lordship

6.meaning: 'And the meeting with Him' — the verbal noun for encountering or coming face to face; joined to 'Him', it denotes the encounter with one's Lord.
6.grammar: A verbal noun with the attached possessive -hi ('Him/His'). The -i vowel before the suffix is the genitive case — the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to another noun ('… of …'); the suffix appears as -hi (rather than -hu) precisely because of that -i vowel. The wa- prefix means 'and'.

7.meaning: 'So it came to nothing / fell flat / was rendered void' — said of deeds that are nullified and lose all worth, like a body that swells up and perishes; the effort comes to ruin.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -at ending (the feminine -t suffix on the past-tense stem) marks a feminine 'she/it' as the subject — Arabic plurals of non-rational things are treated as feminine singular — giving 'it became void'. The fa- prefix means 'so/then', marking a consequence.
7.root: ح-ب-ط (ḥ-b-ṭ) — coming to nothing, deeds being nullified

8.meaning: Their deeds / works / actions — the things they have done.
8.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'deed', meaning 'deeds/works'. The attached -hum means 'their' (masculine plural), forming a possessive link. The -u before the pronoun is nominative, marking the whole phrase ('their deeds') as a subject. The -hum form keeps its u-vowel after this nominative ending.

9.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
9.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

10.meaning: 'We set up / establish / assign' — to make something stand upright and firm, to set it in place; with a following word like 'weight' it means to give or accord measure to it.
10.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (the 'make/cause' pattern meaning 'to make stand, to set up'). Form IV is identified by its stem shape — a ḍamma on the imperfect prefix with the middle weak letter resolving as a long ī (nu-qīm-) — not by the prefix letter alone, since the n- prefix is just the ordinary 1st-person-plural marker shared by every verb form. The nu- prefix marks 'we' as the doers, and the -u mood-vowel at the end is the plain indicative, used for a simple statement of action.
10.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — standing, rising, setting upright

11.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
11.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

12.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
12.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
12.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

13.meaning: "the Resurrection" — the standing-up of all people from death to be judged; literally the act of rising or standing up.
13.grammar: The al- prefix means "the." The -i ending (on the feminine -t) is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ("the … OF this") or follows a preposition.
13.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise

14.meaning: 'A weight / weighing' — the verbal noun for what something weighs, its heft or measured worth; by extension, value or consequence.
14.grammar: A verbal noun ('a weight') preceded by wa- ('and'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb — here the thing that is given or set.

1.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
1.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

2.meaning: 'Their recompense / requital / reward' — the return or payment one is given in response to deeds, whether good or bad. Combined here with 'their.'
2.grammar: A noun with the attached possessive -hum ('their,' masculine plural). The -u vowel on 'jazāʾ' is the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or the thing being identified in a statement.
2.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to recompense, repay, requite

3.meaning: Hell / Jahannam — the proper name of the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter.
3.grammar: A proper name (the name of Hell), treated as a feminine, non-fully-inflecting noun. The final -u is the nominative case ending, marking it as the subject/predicate of a statement ('… is Jahannam'). Because it is a proper name of this type, it does not take the usual final '-n' (tanwīn) of ordinary nouns.

4.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
4.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

5.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
5.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

6.meaning: and they took / adopted (for themselves); a verb for taking something up, seizing it, or adopting it as one's own.
6.grammar: Past-tense verb in the self-directed pattern (Form VIII), which adds the sense of doing the action for oneself — taking or adopting something to oneself. The -ū ending marks a completed action done by a masculine plural subject ('they took'). The silent alif written after it is a spelling convention for this plural ending.

7.meaning: My signs / My verses — clear tokens, proofs, or revealed verses that point to a truth, here belonging to the speaker ('My').
7.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun ('signs') with the attached possessive -ī meaning 'my'. The plural is built with the -āt ending; the long -ī suffix marks first-person singular ownership.
7.root: ا-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

8.meaning: 'And My messengers' — the plural of 'messenger' or 'envoy', one sent with a message; joined to 'My', it denotes the messengers belonging to the speaker.
8.grammar: A plural noun with the attached possessive -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending fixes the word's form, so it reads simply 'my messengers'. The wa- prefix means 'and'.

9.meaning: Mockery, ridicule, a laughing-stock — the act of deriding, or an object treated as a joke. Huzuw is scornful jesting that belittles.
9.grammar: An indefinite verbal noun in the accusative ('an' written with tanwīn on a final alif). The accusative here is typical for the object of a verb or for stating what something is taken/treated 'as'. 'Indefinite' means 'mockery / a mockery' rather than 'the mockery'.
9.root: ه-ز-و (h-z-w) — to mock, ridicule, scoff at; a wāw-final variant of the related root ه-ز-أ (h-z-ʾ), this written form ending in wāw

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + 'they did / worked / performed.' The verb denotes doing deeds, working, putting effort into action — practical doing as opposed to mere speaking or believing.
4.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + a past-tense verb, 3rd person masculine plural. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and they did / worked.'

5.meaning: 'The righteous deeds / good works' — the definite plural of a word meaning that which is sound, wholesome, upright, and beneficial. As a noun it refers to good, virtuous actions that set things right.
5.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun ('the good deeds'). The -i ending is the oblique case used by feminine plurals to mark either the genitive ('… of …' / after a preposition) or the accusative (direct object); for this plural pattern the accusative and genitive share the same -i ending.
5.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

6.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'she was / it was / it became' — from the core verb of being, linking a subject to a description or state, often setting it in past or established time.
6.grammar: A completed (past-tense) verb of being. The ending -at marks a third-person feminine-singular subject, 'she' or 'it (feminine)', so it reads 'she/it was'. As a being-verb it normally introduces a description of that subject.
6.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

7.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
7.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

8.meaning: Gardens — lush, densely shaded enclosures whose foliage covers the ground; the plural of the word for a garden, used pre-eminently for the Gardens of Paradise.
8.grammar: A feminine sound plural of 'janna' (garden), formed with the '-āt' plural ending. The final '-u' is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun that simply names or identifies something ('… are gardens').
8.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — covering, concealing; lush garden whose growth covers the earth

9.meaning: 'The Firdaws' — the loftiest and most spacious garden, the highest and most excellent part of Paradise; a lush enclosed garden of every kind.
9.grammar: A definite noun ('the Firdaws') with the prefix 'the'. The -i ending is the genitive case — the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
9.root: — (no triliteral Arabic root; a borrowed word for the highest garden of Paradise)

10.meaning: An offering of welcome, a lodging prepared for a guest, or a hospitable provision laid out on arrival.
10.grammar: A masculine noun, indefinite. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks the accusative, commonly used here for an object or in an explanatory sense ('as a welcome-gift').
10.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — descending, alighting, being a guest

1.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
1.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.

2.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
2.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
2.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: 'They seek / desire / pursue.' It conveys actively wanting and going after something, sometimes with a sense of craving or even wrongful overreaching.
4.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb. The ya-…-ūna pattern marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, the default form used for plain statements of fact.
4.root: ب-غ-ي (b-gh-y) — to seek, desire; to overreach, transgress

5.meaning: From it / about it / away from it — a preposition meaning 'from' or 'off of', attached to a feminine 'it'.
5.grammar: 'ʿan' is a preposition conveying departure or removal — 'away from / off of / concerning'. The attached -hā is 'it/her', referring to a single feminine thing. Prepositions like this put the following pronoun in the genitive.

6.meaning: A turning-away or shifting from one place or state to another; a transfer, change, or moving elsewhere. The pattern conveys the act or result of seeking to be removed or relocated from something.
6.grammar: A masculine singular indefinite noun. The final -an (written with tanwīn, 'an') is the indefinite accusative: it marks the word as 'a/some …' and signals that it functions as an object of a verb (something acted upon, sought, or denied), rather than as the subject.
6.root: ح-و-ل (ḥ-w-l) — turning, shifting, changing, transferring from one state or place to another

1.meaning: An imperative command meaning 'Say!' or 'Speak!' — a direct order to one person to utter or declare something.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a single male. The bare, vowelless ending (the silent stop on the final 'l') marks it as a direct order: 'you, say!' It is built from the verb 'to say' with the weak middle letter dropped, leaving the short, clipped command form.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak, to utter

2.meaning: If — a conditional particle introducing a hypothetical that is contrary to fact or unfulfilled ("if [such-and-such had been the case]…"), typically implying that because the condition did not hold, its result did not occur either.
2.grammar: A conditional particle. It has no ending to inflect. It sets up a supposed condition, classically one understood as unreal or unrealized, and is normally answered by a result clause (often introduced by la-, "surely [then]…").

3.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

3.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

4.meaning: The sea or large body of water; a vast expanse of deep water. By extension it can suggest anything immense or abundant.
4.grammar: A masculine singular noun made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing or being something).
4.root: ب-ح-ر (b-ḥ-r) — sea, vast expanse of water; depth and abundance

5.meaning: Ink — the writing fluid used with a pen; more broadly any material supplied to keep something going, the substance that feeds writing.
5.grammar: A masculine singular indefinite noun. The final -an (tanwīn, 'an') is the indefinite accusative: it marks the word as 'some/an …' and commonly indicates the object of a verb or a noun used to specify in what respect something is so (e.g. 'as ink').
5.root: م-د-د (m-d-d) — extending, supplying, replenishing; a steady flow or supply

6.meaning: Belonging to, or for the sake of, the words/utterances — specifically denoting 'words' in the plural. Kalimāt are spoken or decreed words, statements, and by extension the decrees, signs, and creative commands of Allah.
6.grammar: A feminine sound plural noun ('words') preceded by the preposition li- ('for, belonging to'). The -āt is the feminine plural marker, and the final -i is the genitive ending, required here because the noun follows the preposition li- ('for …').

7.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
7.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
7.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

8.meaning: It would surely run out, be used up, or come to an end through being depleted. The verb expresses something being exhausted or running dry.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('it ran out / was depleted'), with the emphatic prefix la- ('surely, certainly'). The final -a is the standard ending for 'he/it' in the past tense. The la- prefix often appears in the answer to a conditional ('… would surely …').
8.root: ن-ف-د (n-f-d) — running out, being exhausted, coming to an end of a supply

9.meaning: The sea or large body of water; a vast expanse of deep water. By extension it can suggest anything immense or abundant.
9.grammar: A masculine singular noun made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing or being something).
9.root: ب-ح-ر (b-ḥ-r) — sea, vast expanse of water; depth and abundance

10.meaning: An adverb of time and place meaning 'before' — denoting what comes prior to something else, whether earlier in time or ahead of it in sequence.
10.grammar: An adverb of time/place ending in -a. It is regularly placed before a following noun to mean 'before that thing' (e.g. 'before X'), functioning much like a preposition that the next word completes.
10.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, to come before; the front/fore

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
11.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
11.root: — (particle; no root)

12.meaning: It runs out, becomes exhausted, or comes to an end — the act of being depleted, expressed as an ongoing or potential event.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ta- prefix marking a feminine singular ('it/she') subject. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which appears after certain particles (such as 'that', 'before', or 'until') and gives the sense 'that it run out' or 'before it runs out', rather than a plain statement of fact.
12.root: ن-ف-د (n-f-d) — running out, being exhausted, coming to an end of a supply

13.meaning: Words, utterances, statements — the plural of 'word'. In divine usage, the kalimāt are Allah's decrees, creative commands, signs, and promises, regarded as inexhaustible.
13.grammar: A feminine sound plural noun ('words'). The -āt is the feminine plural marker, and the final -u is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing or being something).
13.root: ك-ل-م (k-l-m) — speech, word, utterance

14.meaning: 'My Lord' — the Master, Sustainer and Nurturer, claimed in close personal relation by the speaker.
14.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord') with the attached pronoun -ī meaning 'my'. This 'my' ending merges with the case-vowel of the noun, so a single long -ī is heard. The sense is 'the Lord who is mine'.
14.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord/master, to nurture and sustain

15.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
15.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').
15.root: — (particles; no triliteral root)

16.meaning: We came / We brought — to arrive, or to bring something forward and present it.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix '-nā' is the subject ending meaning 'we (did it),' marking a completed action performed by a first-person plural — something already brought about.
16.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — coming, arriving; bringing forth

17.meaning: With the like of it — 'the like, equal, or similar' of something, joined to a preposition meaning 'with/by'. Mithl denotes a counterpart or match, something of the same kind.
17.grammar: The noun mithl ('like, equal') preceded by the preposition bi- ('with, by') and followed by the attached pronoun -hi ('its / of it'). The -i ending is genitive, required after the preposition bi-; the pronoun -hi likewise takes the -i form because it follows a genitive word.
17.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, resemblance; a match or equal

18.meaning: A reinforcement, supply, or supplement; an addition that extends or replenishes something, providing more support or help to sustain it.
18.grammar: A masculine singular indefinite noun. The final -an (tanwīn, 'an') is the indefinite accusative: it marks the word as 'a/some …' and here commonly functions to specify in what respect (e.g. 'as a supplement / by way of reinforcement').
18.root: م-د-د (m-d-d) — extending, supplying, reinforcing; a steady flow or supply

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
2.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

3.meaning: I — the standalone pronoun used to declare or emphasize the speaker himself as the one in view.
3.grammar: A detached first-person singular pronoun ("I"). Being an independent pronoun, it has a fixed form with no case ending; it is used to state or stress who the subject is.

4.meaning: 'A human being, a mortal man' — bashar denotes humankind as flesh-and-blood mortals. It emphasizes the human, bodily nature of a person.
4.grammar: A noun (also usable collectively for 'mankind'). The -un ending is nominative with tanwīn (nunation — the doubled 'n' sound marking an indefinite noun, 'a human being'). The nominative case marks it as the subject of a sentence (e.g. the one who acts) or as a noun whose existence is being affirmed or denied.

5.meaning: One like you, your equal, of the same kind as you (addressing a group) — 'a like' or 'counterpart' joined to the plural 'you'. It asserts sameness of nature.
5.grammar: The noun mithl ('like, equal') with the attached pronoun -kum ('you', addressing a group of males or a mixed group). The -u ending is nominative, typically marking the word as the subject or as a predicate ('… is one like you').
5.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — likeness, similarity, resemblance; a match or equal

6.meaning: 'It is revealed / inspired' — for a message to be conveyed by Allah to a prophet, whether by inspiration, sign, or revealed word. This is the passive sense: the revelation is sent to the recipient.

parts.en: he/it (third-person masculine present prefix, passive vowel)
is revealed / inspired (passive stem ending in a long final vowel)

6.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice: the 'yu-' prefix with the internal vowel pattern means 'it is (being) revealed' — the action is done TO the subject. The verb ends in a fixed long '-ā' vowel because its final root letter is weak; this form is the same in the passive present regardless of case.
6.root: و-ح-ي (w-ḥ-y) — revelation, inspiration, conveying a message

7.meaning: 'To me / toward me.' It joins the preposition ilā, meaning 'to / toward,' with an attached first-person 'me,' expressing motion or direction toward the speaker.
7.grammar: A preposition meaning 'to / toward' with the attached pronoun 'me.' The base preposition is ilā, ending in a long vowel (written with alif maqsūra, ى). When the 'me' pronoun attaches, that final long vowel turns into yāʾ and merges with the pronoun's yāʾ, giving a doubled, stressed -ayya — the whole word reading ilayya, 'to me.'

8.meaning: A compound particle meaning 'that …' or 'only that' — it introduces and emphasizes a fact as the content of a thought or statement; 'anna' asserts ('indeed/that') and the attached 'mā' often gives a restrictive sense ('that … is only …').
8.grammar: A combination of the emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with 'mā'. 'Anna' introduces a noun-clause as the object of verbs like 'think' or 'know', putting the following noun in the accusative. Joined with 'mā' it frequently carries a limiting force, 'only/merely'. Particles like this do not themselves take case endings.

9.meaning: Your god/deity (addressing a group) — the one deemed worthy of worship, the object of devotion. Ilāh denotes 'a god, an object of worship'; with -kum it means 'your god'.
9.grammar: The noun ilāh ('god, deity') with the attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your', addressing a group). The -u ending is nominative, typically marking the word as the subject of a sentence or as a predicate ('your god is …').
9.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, divinity; being worshipped and turned to in devotion

10.meaning: A god / an object of worship — a being taken as a deity and worshipped. As an indefinite noun it means 'a god' in the general sense.
10.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a god') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
10.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

11.meaning: One / single and unique — denoting oneness: a single individual, undivided and without partner or plurality.
11.grammar: An adjective/numeral meaning 'one.' The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the nominative case, the case typically used for a subject, predicate, or a descriptor agreeing with such a noun.
11.root: و-ح-د (w-ḥ-d) — oneness, singularity, uniqueness

12.meaning: A compound meaning 'then whoever' or 'so whoever'. It combines 'then/so' with the conditional/relative 'who', introducing whatever person meets a stated condition.
12.grammar: The connector fa- ('then/so', often answering or following a condition) joined to man ('whoever / the one who'), which refers to people and introduces a condition: 'whoever does X…'. man does not change its ending; the clause after it supplies the rest of the meaning.

13.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

13.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
13.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

14.meaning: He hopes for, looks forward to, or expectantly desires something good; it can also carry the nuance of awe or fearful expectation. The verb blends hopeful longing with anticipation of what is to come.

parts.en: spelling alif after the long ū

14.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he hopes'). The ya- prefix marks the 'he' subject; the stem ends in a long -ū. The written alif at the end is a spelling convention (it is not pronounced) and does not change the meaning. The form describes an ongoing or habitual action.
14.root: ر-ج-و (r-j-w) — hoping, expecting, looking forward to good

15.meaning: Meeting, encounter, or coming-face-to-face — the event of two parties meeting, often used of the encounter with one's Lord or an appointed reckoning.
15.grammar: A verbal noun (the act of meeting) on the 'fiʿāl' pattern. The final -a is the accusative case ending, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into that case.
15.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, encounter, come upon

16.meaning: His Lord, Master, and Sustainer — the One who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to completion; expressing both ownership and loving care over the one belonging to Him.
16.grammar: A masculine noun with an attached possessive pronoun ("his Lord"). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, here drawn out because of the following possessive suffix -hi ("his"). The suffix -hi means "his," and its i-form follows naturally after an i-vowel.
16.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

17.meaning: Then let him do / act — a command directed at a third party ('let him…'), built on the verb 'to do, work, act, perform deeds'.
17.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular, turned into a command by the prefixed particle l- ('let him…'), with the connector fa- ('so, then') at the front. Because of this 'let him' particle the verb is in the jussive mood, shown by the absence of a final vowel on the last letter — giving the sense of an order or exhortation ('let him do').
17.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — doing, working, acting; performing deeds

18.meaning: A deed / an action — a thing done, a work or act performed. The word names the action itself, stated indefinitely ('a deed').
18.grammar: A noun, 'deed/work/action'. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a deed') and accusative in case — the form typically used for the object of a verb or to specify 'as/in respect of'.
18.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; a deed

19.meaning: "Righteous / good / sound" — an active participle describing one who or that which is upright and wholesome and acts rightly; as a description of deeds it means good, virtuous works.
19.grammar: An active participle used as a noun or adjective. The -an ending (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a righteous one / a good deed') and in the accusative case — the form used for a direct object or other complement.
19.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound / upright / righteous

20.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
20.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

21.meaning: He associates a partner (with someone), ascribes an equal or sharer — especially setting up partners alongside Allah. The verb denotes making something a partner or sharer in what belongs to one alone.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular, in the causative (form IV) pattern ('he makes/takes as a partner'). The yu- prefix marks the 'he' subject. The final letter carries no vowel (jussive mood), which occurs after certain particles such as the negative 'not' or 'let' — so the plain dictionary sense is 'he associates partners'.
21.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — sharing, partnership; associating a partner or equal

22.meaning: In/with the worship of — 'worship, service, devotion' joined to the preposition 'with/in'. ʿIbādah is the humble service and devotion owed to the One worshipped, encompassing reverence, obedience, and submission.
22.grammar: A feminine singular verbal noun ('worship') preceded by the preposition bi- ('in, with'). The final -i is the genitive ending, required because the noun follows the preposition bi-. Being a genitive, it also typically links to a following noun, giving the sense 'in the worship OF …'.
22.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — worship, service, devotion; humble submission to the one served

23.meaning: His Lord, Master, and Sustainer — the One who owns, nurtures, governs, and brings to completion; expressing both ownership and loving care over the one belonging to Him.
23.grammar: A masculine noun with an attached possessive pronoun ("his Lord"). The -i vowel on the noun is genitive, here drawn out because of the following possessive suffix -hi ("his"). The suffix -hi means "his," and its i-form follows naturally after an i-vowel.
23.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship, ownership, nurturing and sustaining to completion

24.meaning: One; a single one; anyone — and in negative/prohibitive contexts, 'anyone at all / no one.'
24.grammar: A noun meaning 'one/anyone.' The '-an' ending (indefinite 'tanwīn') is the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb ('ask anyone'). When such a verb is negated or prohibited, 'aḥadan' carries the sense 'anyone at all.' The indefiniteness comes from the nunation.
